+`GET /health` is liveness only — the process serves. `GET /ready` is the honest readiness signal `make local` polls: `200 {"ready": true}` once the pipeline produces, `503 {"ready": false, "reason": <string>}` otherwise. Reasons in precedence order: `status_error` (the served status is `level:"error"`), `runtime_not_started`, `models_not_loaded`, `no_recent_gaze`. A paused tracker counts as ready — pausing stops the stream on purpose — and fresh gaze means `gaze.updated_at` within the last 3s.
+
+The GET endpoints are read-only; `POST /control` is the single write path. Its JSON body is `{"action": "<name>", "value": <any>}` where `action` is one of `pause_toggle`, `recalibrate`, `dot_scale`, `dwell_lock`, `preview_toggle`, `status_toggle`, `inference_time_toggle`, `show_marker`, `implicit_sample`, or `quit`. Response codes:
+
+- `200 {"ok": true}` — a valid non-lifecycle action forwarded to the renderer (`recalibrate` runs the same path as the `⌘⇧G` hotkey).
+- `202 {"ok": true}` — `quit` only: acknowledged API-side, then the app quits on the next tick; it is never forwarded to the renderer.
+- `400` — `bad_request` (unparseable request target), `unknown_action`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_body`, or `invalid_value`. `invalid_value` is specific to `implicit_sample`: its `value` must be a normalized screen point `{"x_norm": 0..1, "y_norm": 0..1}` — a malformed point is rejected here rather than clamped into a bogus calibration label.
+- `409 {"error": "tracking_inactive"}` — `implicit_sample` declined because no live inference can consume the label (renderer down, modal UI owning the screen, tracker paused, or models never reported loaded). On accept it lands as the same `cursor_idle` message the idle sampler emits.
+- `405` — non-POST on `/control`, non-GET elsewhere. `403` — requests carrying an `Origin` header are rejected: the API is unauthenticated, so only originless local clients may call it. `413` — body over 64 KiB. `503 control_unavailable` — no control/quit handler wired (e.g. `quit` without an `onQuit` callback). Handlers may also return their own `{status, error}` 4xx/5xx result.

+## Tray & Settings
+
+In standalone runs (no `--no-tray`), a menu-bar tray icon shows the tracker state (`Tracking` / `Paused` / `No face` / `Calibrating` / `Needs calibration`) and offers `Recalibrate` (same path as `⌘⇧G`), a `Pause Tracking` / `Resume Tracking` toggle (same as `⌘⇧P`), dot-size and dwell-lock controls, diagnostic toggles (preview, status panel, inference time), and `Quit`.
+
+User-facing toggles persist to `settings.json`, written next to the calibration file (so a custom `--calibration-file` puts settings beside it). The file is created on first write; a missing or corrupt file is treated as `{}`. Shape:
+
+```json
+{
+  "version": 1,
+  "dot_scale": 1.0,
+  "dwell_lock": false,
+  "show_camera_marker_on_start": false,
+  "diagnostics": {
+    "preview": false,
+    "status": false,
+    "inference_time": false
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The renderer reads it through the `getSettings`/`setSettings` bridge and reports live state (`paused`, `calibration_status`, `settings`) back through `reportState`, which is what the `/snapshot` slices above expose.

-## 9-Point Calibration
+## Pursuit Calibration
 
-The app can run without calibration. To calibrate, start it with `--calibrate`.
+The app can run without calibration. To calibrate, start it with `--calibrate` — or press `⌘⇧G` at any time for a quick patch.
 
 ```bash
-pnpm dev -- --backend cuda --calibrate
+pnpm dev -- --calibrate
 ```

-After a centered `3`, `2`, `1` countdown, nine calibration targets (center, four corners, and four edge midpoints) and then two separate validation targets appear. For the center target, two red arrows bracket the target as `-> O <-`. For outer targets, a red arrow at the screen center points toward the target direction. Look at each target and hold still with your eyes open. The app takes the median of at least three fresh gaze feature samples near the end of each target display; each sample carries the projected point, per-eye angles, eye centers, head width, iris diameter, and eye openness. Moving, stale, or closed-eye samples are rejected and retried.
+Calibration is a *pursuit* tour: a target glides through waypoints while the app continuously samples the gaze feature stream and tags each frame with the target's interpolated position — no hold-still-and-stare per point. Three tiers trade coverage for time (`--calibration-tier`):
+
+- `full` (default): 17-waypoint 4×4 grid including deep corners — the corners are where iris signal is thinnest, so they get real training data rather than extrapolation.
+- `standard`: 9-waypoint 3×3 grid.
+- `quick`: corners + center, ~10s. This is what `⌘⇧G` runs — a patch for a drifted or moved setup, refitted against the persisted sample pool rather than the 5 new points alone.
+
+After the tour, a verification sweep samples a second pass and gates the fit on median / p90 reprojection error; a failing gate retries without replacing a previous saved calibration.
+
+The fit itself runs a regularized linear map over a ~40-dim feature vector (eye angles, head-pose proxies, iris-in-box offsets, mesh geometry, head-frame position, jaw-delta, and the optional appearance-model yaw/pitch), falling back to affine+RBF when the feature map doesn't earn its complexity on leave-one-out error. The choice is stored in the calibration file (`featuremap-v3` format) along with fitted geometry weights, raw input bounds, verify verdict, an optional drift offset, and up to ~800 feature samples.
 
-When all nine samples are collected, the fit runs two stages. First, a geometry stage re-projects every stored feature across a grid of eye-position weight candidates and keeps the weight pair whose affine fit has the lowest error — this personalizes the head-translation correction to the actual camera mounting instead of the default `1.0/0.25` weights. Second, a 2D affine plus Gaussian RBF residual correction is fitted to the nine re-projected targets to absorb nonlinear projection error that affine alone cannot model. The combined correction is then checked against the two held-out validation targets before it is saved to `.gaze_calibration.json`. If raw targets collapse together, the fit error exceeds `0.18`, or validation fails, the sequence restarts without replacing a previous saved calibration. The fitted eye-position weights are stored in the calibration file (`unclipped-v2` format) and applied to the live projector on load. The 0.06 stability and 0.18 normalized error limits are starting heuristics, not measured accuracy claims.
+**Continuous learning**: when the OS cursor sits idle while your gaze dwells on it, the tracker treats that agreement as a trusted label and refits silently in the background — the map keeps improving the longer you use it, and the sample pool persists across restarts.
 
-When `--calibrate` is used, the PiP camera preview and normal red gaze marker are hidden during calibration and validation. They return after calibration completes.
+**Drift self-healing**: consistent one-directional rejection of implicit labels is read as a camera/laptop move; the measured offset is applied as a persistent `output_offset` so tracking stays correct without a recalibration prompt, then absorbed into the map by the next implicit refit. Only a saturated correction (something beyond a reposition) surfaces the `⌘⇧G` notice.
 
-Calibration files created with clipped raw projection are preserved but ignored; run `--calibrate` to replace one with a validated unclipped calibration. Older `unclipped-v1` files (5-point affine) still load, but they carry no fitted geometry or RBF correction, so recalibrating is recommended. New calibration files store raw input bounds and suppress strong extrapolation outside the calibrated range. The validation errors are saved in the calibration file in normalized display coordinates. They indicate whether the fit met this app's gate; they do not establish pixel accuracy or performance under head movement.
+**Exit**: during calibration or the accuracy test, the `×` button (top-right) or `Escape` cancels cleanly — nothing partial is written.
 
-The live marker also discards a single raw jump larger than 0.35 normalized screen units unless a nearby second frame confirms the new position. This can delay a large intentional glance by one frame. Frames where the model's eye-openness measure indicates a blink are gated out before the jump gate, so blinks no longer inject outlier points; the marker freezes at its last position and dims while eyes are closed. Output smoothing defaults to a One Euro filter (speed-adaptive cutoff), which reduces both idle jitter and fast-glance lag compared with fixed-alpha EMA; `--gaze-filter ema` restores the previous behavior. The calibration and validation flow follows [Tobii's calibration guidance](https://www.developer.tobiipro.com/commonconcepts/calibration.html); the jump thresholds are local heuristics and still need a live comparison of jitter and response delay.
+The live marker gates out blink frames (freezing at the last position while eyes are closed and ~140ms after reopening), passes saccades through unfiltered, and anchors sustained fixations — the default `saccade` filter. `--gaze-filter oneeuro`/`ema` restore the older filters.  ## Estimation Assumptions
 
-- Camera input defaults to `VGA` (`640x480`) and can be changed with `--camera-resolution`. Horizontal FOV defaults to `90°` and can be changed with `--camera-fov`.
+- Camera input defaults to `HD`/`720p` (`1280x720`) with a warned `VGA` (`640x480`) fallback when the device refuses, and can be changed with `--camera-resolution`. Horizontal FOV defaults to `90°` and can be changed with `--camera-fov`.
 - The camera is assumed to be mounted at the top center of the target display.
 - For the vertical direction, the app estimates eye height relative to the camera center from the face/eye bbox Y position and projects it to screen coordinates assuming the camera is at the top center of the display. +function readRequestBody(request, limit = 64 * 1024) {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const chunks = [];
+    let size = 0;
+    request.on("data", (chunk) => {
+      size += chunk.length;

+        // drops the socket, so clients see a JSON error not ECONNRESET.

+  // Cross-process shared state — arrives via the renderer's report-state IPC
+  // and the main-side set-paused/set-settings writers rather than as typed
+  // backend messages. Only keys present in the report are touched, and only
+  // slices whose value actually changed notify subscribers.
+  updateSharedState(report) {
+    if (!report || typeof report !== "object") {
+      return [];
+    }
+    const updatedAt = this.now();
+    const changed = new Set();
+
+    if (report.paused !== undefined) {
+      const paused = Boolean(report.paused);
+      if (this.state.paused !== paused) {
+        this.state.paused = paused;
+        changed.add("paused");
+      }
+    }
+    if (report.calibration_status !== undefined) {
+      const status =
+        report.calibration_status === null ? null : (stringValue(report.calibration_status) ?? null);
+      if (this.state.calibration_status !== status) {
+        this.state.calibration_status = status;
+        changed.add("calibration_status");
+      }
+    }
+    if (report.settings !== undefined) {
+      const settings =
+        report.settings && typeof report.settings === "object" && !Array.isArray(report.settings)
+          ? clone(report.settings)
+          : null;
+      if (JSON.stringify(this.state.settings) !== JSON.stringify(settings)) {
+        this.state.settings = settings;
+        changed.add("settings");
+      }
+    }
+
+    if (changed.size === 0) {
+      return [];
+    }
+    this.state.updated_at = updatedAt;
+    const changedList = Array.from(changed);
+    this.notify(changedList);
+    return changedList;
+  }

+// settings.json merge semantics shared by the set-settings IPC, the tray
+// menu, and POST /control writers: top-level keys overwrite, nested plain
+// objects (diagnostics) merge key-by-key so one toggle can't clobber others.
+function mergeSettings(base, patch) {
+  const merged = { ...(base && typeof base === "object" && !Array.isArray(base) ? base : {}) };
+  if (!patch || typeof patch !== "object" || Array.isArray(patch)) {
+    return merged;
+  }
+  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(patch)) {
+    const existing = merged[key];
+    if (
+      value &&
+      typeof value === "object" &&
+      !Array.isArray(value) &&
+      existing &&
+      typeof existing === "object" &&
+      !Array.isArray(existing)
+    ) {
+      merged[key] = { ...existing, ...value };
+    } else {
+      merged[key] = value;
+    }
+  }
+  return merged;
+}
+
+// Missing/corrupt settings.json is a normal state (first run, truncated
+// write) — callers always get a plain object, never a throw.
+function parseSettingsPayload(text) {
+  if (!text) {
+    return {};
+  }
+  try {
+    const parsed = JSON.parse(text);
+    return parsed && typeof parsed === "object" && !Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : {};
+  } catch {
+    return {};
+  }
+}

+function requestRecalibration(source) {

+function handleControlAction(action, value) {
+  if (action === "recalibrate") {
+    requestRecalibration("control api");
+    return;
+  }
+  // set_paused carries the target state (the host's screen-lock parking),
+  // not a toggle — the renderer applies it through the same path a manual
+  // pause uses and reports it back through set-paused / report-state.
+  if (action === "set_paused") {
+    dispatchMenuAction("set_paused", Boolean(value));
+    return;
+  }
+  // Quit is a lifecycle action, not a renderer menu action — handle it here
+  // whether the API layer routes it through onControl or a dedicated hook.
+  if (action === "quit") {
+    app.quit();
+    return;
+  }
+  if (action === "implicit_sample") {
+    // The host's commit-time implicit label — forwarded as the same
+    // cursor_idle message the idle sampler emits, so the renderer feeds it
+    // through the inference worker's COMETIC quality gate unchanged.
+    // externalApi already range-validates the point; the second check keeps
+    // this entry honest if another caller ever bypasses the HTTP layer.
+    if (!value || !Number.isFinite(value.x_norm) || !Number.isFinite(value.y_norm) ||
+        value.x_norm < 0 || value.x_norm > 1 || value.y_norm < 0 || value.y_norm > 1) {
+      return { status: 400, error: "invalid_value" };
+    }
+    // Decline (409) under the same conditions the sampler stands down — no
+    // live renderer, a modal owning the screen, a paused tracker, or models
+    // that never reported loaded. A label queued behind any of those would
+    // land on stale features or corrupt an in-flight accuracy measurement.
+    const snapshot = gazeStateStore.getSnapshot();
+    const inferenceUp = Boolean(snapshot.runtime?.name && snapshot.models?.detector && snapshot.models?.gaze);
+    if (!mainWindow || mainWindow.isDestroyed() || !rendererReady || modalInteractive || paused || !inferenceUp) {
+      return { status: 409, error: "tracking_inactive" };
+    }
+    sendToRenderer({ type: "cursor_idle", x_norm: value.x_norm, y_norm: value.y_norm }, { updateStore: false });
+    return;
+  }
+  dispatchMenuAction(action, value);
+}

+function persistSettingsPatch(patch) {

+// Freshness bounds for the label — mirrors TrackerControl.swift: a stale
+// preview stamp means the feed froze, and a gaze stamp older than the
+// host's stale window counts as dead air.
+const PREVIEW_STALE_MS = 3000;
+const GAZE_STALE_MS = 1500;
+// First-frame allowance — mirrors the host's 45s gazeGraceWindow: cold
+// shader compiles stay "Starting" inside it, a never-producing pipeline
+// past it is "No gaze", never "Tracking".
+const BOOT_GRACE_MS = 45000;

+function trayStateLabel() {
+  if (paused) {
+    return "Paused";
+  }
+  const calibrationStatus = gazeStateStore.getSlice("calibration_status");
+  if (calibrationStatus === "missing" || calibrationStatus === "invalid") {
+    return "Needs calibration";
+  }
+  if (
+    typeof calibrationStatus === "string" &&
+    calibrationStatus !== "loaded" &&
+    calibrationStatus !== "saved"
+  ) {
+    return "Calibrating";
+  }
+  const preview = gazeStateStore.getSlice("preview");
+  // The preview slice's head claim counts only while its own stamp is
+  // fresh — a frozen preview keeps serving its last answer and would hold
+  // the menu at "Tracking" through a wedge. No stamp keeps the raw claim:
+  // nothing disproves it.
+  const previewStamp = Date.parse(preview?.updated_at ?? "");
+  const previewStale =
+    Number.isFinite(previewStamp) && Date.now() - previewStamp > PREVIEW_STALE_MS;
+  const headDetected = preview && !previewStale ? preview.head_detected : undefined;
+  if (headDetected === false) {
+    return "No face";
+  }
+  const gaze = gazeStateStore.getSlice("gaze");
+  const gazeStamp = Date.parse(gaze?.updated_at ?? "");
+  if (Number.isFinite(gazeStamp)) {
+    if (Date.now() - gazeStamp <= GAZE_STALE_MS) {
+      return "Tracking";
+    }
+    // Feed went quiet — "No gaze" when a face was ever claimed.
+    return headDetected === true || preview?.head_detected === true ? "No gaze" : "No face";
+  }
+  if (headDetected === true) {
+    return "Tracking";
+  }
+  // No gaze stamp, no live face claim — the tracker has never produced a
+  // frame. Inside the boot grace that's still "Starting"; past it (or with
+  // no boot stamp to prove it's still warming) the honest word is "No gaze".
+  const startedStamp = Date.parse(gazeStateStore.getSlice("started_at") ?? "");
+  return Number.isFinite(startedStamp) && Date.now() - startedStamp <= BOOT_GRACE_MS
+    ? "Starting"
+    : "No gaze";
+}

+// Implicit-calibration source (COMETIC/WebGazer): when the cursor rests on a
+// spot inside the calibrated display for a beat, that point is a likely gaze
+// target — emitted once per rest, the worker decides whether to keep it.
+let cursorIdlePoll = null;
+function startCursorIdlePoll(bounds) {
+  let last = { x: Number.NaN, y: Number.NaN };
+  let movedAt = 0;
+  let emitted = false;
+  cursorIdlePoll = setInterval(() => {
+    // modalInteractive/paused: an implicit label mutating the feature map
+    // while the accuracy test scores it corrupts the measurement — and a
+    // paused tracker must not learn from a cursor it isn't driving.
+    if (!mainWindow || mainWindow.isDestroyed() || !rendererReady || modalInteractive || paused) {
+      return;
+    }
+    const point = screen.getCursorScreenPoint();
+    const now = Date.now();
+    if (!Number.isFinite(last.x) || Math.hypot(point.x - last.x, point.y - last.y) > 8) {
+      last = { x: point.x, y: point.y };
+      movedAt = now;
+      emitted = false;
+      return;
+    }
+    if (emitted || now - movedAt < 700) {
+      return;
+    }
+    const xNorm = (point.x - bounds.x) / bounds.width;
+    const yNorm = (point.y - bounds.y) / bounds.height;
+    if (xNorm < 0 || xNorm > 1 || yNorm < 0 || yNorm > 1) {
+      return;
+    }
+    emitted = true;
+    sendToRenderer({ type: "cursor_idle", x_norm: xNorm, y_norm: yNorm }, { updateStore: false });
+  }, 100);
+}

+// Per-path writer mutex: drift-path persistOffset writes can overlap a
+// commitPending save over the same file — plain writeFile can interleave into
+// torn JSON. Chain writes per path and swap in via same-dir rename so the
+// file is always whole.
+const fileWriteQueues = new Map();
+function writeJsonFileAtomic(filePath, payload) {
+  const text = JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2);
+  const previous = fileWriteQueues.get(filePath) || Promise.resolve();
+  const next = previous
+    .catch(() => {})
+    .then(async () => {
+      const tmpPath = `${filePath}.tmp`;
+      await fs.promises.writeFile(tmpPath, text, "utf8");
+      await fs.promises.rename(tmpPath, filePath);
+    });
+  fileWriteQueues.set(filePath, next);
+  const cleanup = () => {
+    if (fileWriteQueues.get(filePath) === next) {
+      fileWriteQueues.delete(filePath);
+    }
+  };
+  next.then(cleanup, cleanup);
+  return next;
+}

+        } else {

+      } catch {

+      }
+    }

+// GET whatever owns the port once. Our own leftover dev server serves
+// index.html referencing /@vite/client; a foreign process squatting on the
+// port does not. Both cases exit 1 — this only decides which story the
+// error message tells.
+function portServesVite() {
+  return new Promise((resolve) => {
+    const request = http.get(devServerUrl, (response) => {
+      let body = "";
+      response.setEncoding("utf8");
+      response.on("data", (chunk) => {
+        body += chunk;
+        if (body.length > 64 * 1024) {
+          request.destroy();
+        }
+      });
+      response.on("end", () => resolve(body.includes("/@vite/client")));
+      response.on("error", () => resolve(false));
+    });
+    request.on("error", () => resolve(false));
+    request.setTimeout(2000, () => {
+      request.destroy();
+      resolve(false);
+    });
+  });
+}

+interface AccuracyBucket {

+  collectFrom: number;
+  errors: number[];
+  inference: number[];
+  intervals: number[];

+function percentile(sorted: number[], q: number): number {
+  return sorted[Math.min(sorted.length - 1, Math.floor(sorted.length * q))];

+function buildPursuitTimeline(
+  waypoints: [number, number][],
+  speed: number,
+  dwellMs: number,
+  leadInMs: number
+): {
+  duration: number;
+  at: (ms: number) => { pos: [number, number] | null; dwelling: boolean; next: [number, number] | null };
+} {
+  const segments: Array<{ start: number; end: number; dwellEnd: number; from: [number, number]; to: [number, number] }> = [];
+  let t = leadInMs;
+  for (let i = 0; i < waypoints.length - 1; i += 1) {
+    const from = waypoints[i];
+    const to = waypoints[i + 1];
+    const travel = (Math.hypot(to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1]) / speed) * 1000;
+    segments.push({ start: t, end: t + travel, dwellEnd: t + travel + dwellMs, from, to });
+    t += travel + dwellMs;
+  }
+  const duration = t;
+  const at = (ms: number): { pos: [number, number] | null; dwelling: boolean; next: [number, number] | null } => {
+    const done = { pos: null, dwelling: false, next: null };
+    if (ms >= duration) {
+      return done;
+    }
+    for (let i = 0; i < segments.length; i += 1) {
+      const s = segments[i];
+      const upcoming = segments[i + 1]?.to ?? null;
+      if (ms < s.start) {
+        // Parked at this leg's origin; `next` shows where it goes next.
+        return { pos: s.from, dwelling: true, next: s.to };
+      }
+      if (ms <= s.end) {
+        const k = (ms - s.start) / (s.end - s.start);
+        // Smoothstep glide: soft acceleration into the park, never a dart.
+        const e = k * k * (3 - 2 * k);
+        return { pos: [s.from[0] + (s.to[0] - s.from[0]) * e, s.from[1] + (s.to[1] - s.from[1]) * e], dwelling: false, next: upcoming };
+      }
+      if (ms < s.dwellEnd) {
+        return { pos: s.to, dwelling: true, next: upcoming };
+      }
+    }
+    return { pos: waypoints[waypoints.length - 1], dwelling: true, next: null };
+  };
+  return { duration, at };
+}

+// Render-side velocity: finite difference between gaze frames on the CAPTURE
+// cadence (frame_interval_ms / captured_at_ms), not IPC arrival — transport
+// jitter otherwise reads as motion. Saccade-marked or large-jump frames snap
+// the dot instead of touching the EMA: the eye already arrived, and saccadic
+// suppression makes the teleport invisible. Returns true when it snapped.
+// Runs inside the gaze message handler; the rAF loop only reads the refs.
+function updateGazeMotion(
+  targetRef: { current: [number, number] | null },
+  targetAtRef: { current: number },
+  velRef: { current: [number, number] },
+  xNorm: number,
+  yNorm: number,
+  meta: { gazeState?: string; frameIntervalMs?: number; capturedAtMs?: number } = {}
+): boolean {
+  const next: [number, number] = [xNorm, yNorm];
+  if (!Number.isFinite(next[0]) || !Number.isFinite(next[1])) {
+    // A non-finite frame would poison the velocity EMA permanently (NaN
+    // fails every comparison, so the clamp can never clear it) — drop it.
+    velRef.current = [0, 0];
+    return false;
+  }
+  const prev = targetRef.current;
+  // targetAt carries wall-clock capture time — Date.now() is shared between
+  // the worker and page realms, performance.now() is not.
+  const capturedAt = Number.isFinite(meta.capturedAtMs) ? (meta.capturedAtMs as number) : Date.now();
+  if (isSaccadeJump(meta.gazeState, prev, next)) {
+    velRef.current = [0, 0];
+    targetRef.current = next;
+    targetAtRef.current = capturedAt;
+    return true;
+  }
+  const prevAt = targetAtRef.current;
+  if (prev && prevAt > 0) {
+    const dt = meta.frameIntervalMs && meta.frameIntervalMs > 0
+      ? Math.min(1, meta.frameIntervalMs / 1000)
+      : Math.max(0.001, (capturedAt - prevAt) / 1000);
+    let vx = velRef.current[0] + 0.5 * ((next[0] - prev[0]) / dt - velRef.current[0]);
+    let vy = velRef.current[1] + 0.5 * ((next[1] - prev[1]) / dt - velRef.current[1]);
+    const speed = Math.hypot(vx, vy);
+    if (speed > 4) {
+      vx *= 4 / speed;
+      vy *= 4 / speed;
+    }
+    velRef.current = [vx, vy];
+  }
+  targetRef.current = next;
+  targetAtRef.current = capturedAt;
+  return false;
+}

+// The dedicated-worker path loads its models through runtimes.ts — stub them
+// so the worker module can be exercised end-to-end without onnxruntime.
+// workerModelsControl is read live inside the mock: a test can inject a
+// dead session (detectError), a failing reload (createError / per-accelerator
+// createErrorFor), a rebuilt session that dies on its probe run
+// (warmupFailures), a dispose that never settles (disposeHang), or a detect
+// held on a gate promise (detectGate) without re-mocking. createCalls records
+// every requested accelerator so ladder order is assertable; detectInFlight /
+// maxDetectInFlight prove frames never overlap a shared detect.
+const workerModelsControl = vi.hoisted(() => ({
+  detectError: null as Error | null,
+  createError: null as Error | null,
+  createErrorFor: {} as Record<string, Error | undefined>,
+  warmupFailures: 0,
+  disposeHang: false,
+  detectGate: null as Promise<void> | null,
+  // Override the canned detection wholesale — a head:null result is how the
+  // no-face/away path is driven without re-mocking the module.
+  detectResult: null as { head: unknown; eyes: unknown[]; mouth: unknown } | null,
+  createCalls: [] as string[],
+  detectCalls: 0,
+  detectInFlight: 0,
+  maxDetectInFlight: 0
+}));

+    workerModelsControl.createCalls.push(accelerator);

+    if (createError) {
+      throw createError;
+    }

+        try {

+          if (gate) {
+            await gate;
+          }
+          if (workerModelsControl.detectError) {
+            throw workerModelsControl.detectError;

+describe("metric head pose", () => {
+  // A rigid "face" in camera coords — asymmetric blobs so every rotation
+  // axis is observable (two eye rings, a brow ridge, a chin row).
+  function syntheticHead(): Float32Array {
+    const pts: number[] = [];
+    for (const [cx, cy, cz] of [
+      [-40, -6, 4],
+      [40, -6, 4]
+    ]) {
+      for (let i = 0; i < 24; i += 1) {
+        const a = (i / 24) * Math.PI * 2;
+        pts.push(cx + Math.cos(a) * 14, cy + Math.sin(a) * 8, cz + Math.sin(a * 2) * 4);
+      }
+    }
+    for (let i = 0; i < 16; i += 1) {
+      pts.push(-50 + (100 * i) / 15, -42, 8 + ((i * 7) % 5));
+      pts.push(-50 + (100 * i) / 15, 46, 10 + ((i * 11) % 5));
+    }
+    return new Float32Array(pts);
+  }
+
+  it("recovers known rotations within a fraction of a degree", () => {
+    const reference = syntheticHead();
+    for (const [yaw, pitch, roll] of [
+      [18, -9, 6],
+      [-24, 14, -10],
+      [0, 0, 0],
+      [35, 20, 15]
+    ]) {
+      const rotated = applyPoseRotation(reference, yaw, pitch, roll);
+      // Distance/framing invariance: uniform scale + translation must be
+      // absorbed by the rigid fit.
+      for (let i = 0; i < rotated.length; i += 3) {
+        rotated[i] = rotated[i] * 1.7 + 300;
+        rotated[i + 1] = rotated[i + 1] * 1.7 + 220;
+        rotated[i + 2] = rotated[i + 2] * 1.7 - 15;
+      }
+      const pose = estimateHeadPoseFromMesh(rotated, reference);
+      expect(pose).not.toBeNull();
+      expect(pose!.yawDeg).toBeCloseTo(yaw, 1);
+      expect(pose!.pitchDeg).toBeCloseTo(pitch, 1);
+      expect(pose!.rollDeg).toBeCloseTo(roll, 1);
+    }
+  });
+
+  it("keeps the proxy sign conventions and a ~0 neutral pose", () => {
+    // yaw > 0: a forward (-z) point tips toward image-right (+x) — the
+    // direction the old headYawProxy went when the nose moved right of the
+    // eye midpoint.
+    const yawed = applyPoseRotation(new Float32Array([0, 0, -1]), 20, 0, 0);
+    expect(yawed[0]).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    // pitch > 0: forward tips toward image-down (+y), matching the proxy's
+    // nose-below-eye-line reading.
+    const pitched = applyPoseRotation(new Float32Array([0, 0, -1]), 0, 20, 0);
+    expect(pitched[1]).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    // roll > 0: the +x end of the eye line tips down (+y) — the same sense
+    // as headRollRad's atan2(dy, dx).
+    const rolled = applyPoseRotation(new Float32Array([1, 0, 0]), 0, 0, 20);
+    expect(rolled[1]).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    const reference = syntheticHead();
+    const pose = estimateHeadPoseFromMesh(reference, reference);
+    expect(pose).not.toBeNull();

+  });

+  it("disabling anchorEnabled mid-lock releases the anchor on the next update", () => {
+    const f = new SaccadeAwareGazeFilter();
+    for (let i = 0; i < 14; i += 1) {
+      f.update(0.5 + (i % 3) * 0.002, 0.5, i * 70, 0, 0);
+    }
+    expect(f.dwellLocked).toBe(true);
+    f.anchorEnabled = false;
+    f.update(0.5, 0.5, 15 * 70, 0, 0);
+    expect(f.dwellLocked).toBe(false);
+  });
+
+  it("saccade filter holds the last output on NaN input and never stores it", () => {
+    const f = new SaccadeAwareGazeFilter();
+    expect(f.update(0.5, 0.5, 0, 0, 0)).toEqual([0.5, 0.5]);
+    expect(f.update(Number.NaN, 0.5, 16, 0, 0)).toEqual([0.5, 0.5]);
+    expect(f.update(0.52, 0.5, 32, 0, 0).every(Number.isFinite)).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it("angle smoother holds the last good angles on a NaN frame", () => {
+    const smoother = new GazeAngleSmoother();
+    const estimate: GazeEstimate = {
+      yawDeg: 2,
+      pitchDeg: 1,
+      leftYawDeg: 2,
+      leftPitchDeg: 1,
+      rightYawDeg: 2,
+      rightPitchDeg: 1,
+      irisDiameterPx: 30,
+      eyeOpen: 0.9,
+      agreement: 1
+    };
+    expect(smoother.update(estimate).yawDeg).toBe(2);
+    const held = smoother.update({ ...estimate, leftYawDeg: Number.NaN });
+    expect(held.yawDeg).toBe(2);
+    expect(held.leftYawDeg).toBe(2);
+    const next = smoother.update({ ...estimate, leftYawDeg: 4, rightYawDeg: 4, yawDeg: 4 });
+    expect(Number.isFinite(next.yawDeg)).toBe(true);
+  });
+});

+describe("inference worker", () => {
+  function workerConfig(accelerator: "auto" | "webgpu" | "wasm" = "wasm"): WebInferenceConfig {
+    return {
+      runtime: "onnxweb",
+      webInferenceWorker: "dedicated",
+      webAccelerator: accelerator,
+      detector: "yolo",
+      backend: "web",
+      camera: "0",
+      cameraWidth: 640,
+      cameraHeight: 480,
+      cameraFov: 90,
+      scoreThreshold: 0.5,
+      displaySizeInch: 31.5,
+      displayWidth: 1920,
+      displayHeight: 1080,
+      calibrationFile: "c.json",
+      detectorModel: "det.onnx",
+      lipMotionModel: "lip.onnx",
+      detectorModelUrl: "det.onnx",
+      gazeModelUrl: "gaze.onnx",
+      lipMotionModelUrl: "lip.onnx",
+      onnxWasmBaseUrl: "/",
+      smoothingAlpha: 0.5,
+      smoothingAlphaY: 0.5,
+      calibrate: false,
+      gazeFilter: "saccade",
+      filterMincutoff: 1,
+      filterBeta: 0.7,
+      filterDcutoff: 1,
+      disableIrisDistance: false,
+      previewFps: 5,
+      gazeMaxFps: 30,
+      hidePreview: true,
+      flipX: true,
+      flipY: true,
+      cameraScreenX: 0.5,
+      cameraScreenY: 0,
+      eyePositionWeightX: 1,
+      eyePositionWeightY: 0.25,
+      retinafaceHeadFaceRatio: 1,
+      gazeProjectionMode: "binocular-screen",
+      enableLipMotion: false
+    };
+  }
+
+  // Shared self stub: the worker assigns self.onmessage once at import, so
+  // the same object must serve every test in this file.
+  const workerMessages: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];
+  const selfStub: { onmessage: null | ((event: { data: unknown }) => void); postMessage: (message: unknown) => void } = {
+    onmessage: null,
+    postMessage: (message) => workerMessages.push(message as Record<string, unknown>)
+  };
+
+  async function startWorker(accelerator: "auto" | "webgpu" | "wasm" = "wasm") {
+    // Cross-test hygiene: module state persists between tests in this file —
+    // reset the shared control block before every init.
+    workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+    workerModelsControl.createError = null;
+    workerModelsControl.createErrorFor = {};
+    workerModelsControl.warmupFailures = 0;
+    workerModelsControl.disposeHang = false;
+    workerModelsControl.detectGate = null;
+    workerModelsControl.detectResult = null;
+    workerModelsControl.createCalls = [];
+    workerModelsControl.detectCalls = 0;
+    workerModelsControl.detectInFlight = 0;
+    workerModelsControl.maxDetectInFlight = 0;
+    vi.stubGlobal("self", selfStub);
+    vi.stubGlobal(
+      "ImageData",
+      class {
+        constructor(
+          readonly data: Uint8ClampedArray,
+          readonly width: number,
+          readonly height: number
+        ) {}
+      }
+    );
+    vi.stubGlobal(
+      "OffscreenCanvas",
+      class {
+        constructor(
+          readonly width: number,
+          readonly height: number
+        ) {}
+        getContext() {
+          return {
+            drawImage: () => undefined,
+            putImageData: () => undefined,
+            getImageData: (_x: number, _y: number, w: number, h: number) =>
+              new (globalThis.ImageData as unknown as new (d: Uint8ClampedArray, w: number, h: number) => object)(
+                new Uint8ClampedArray(w * h * 4),
+                w,
+                h
+              )
+          };
+        }
+      }
+    );
+    workerMessages.length = 0;
+    await import("./inferenceWorker");
+    const send = (message: unknown) => selfStub.onmessage?.({ data: message });
+    send({ type: "init", config: workerConfig(accelerator) });
+    // The pump posts camera_geometry the moment getUserMedia answers —
+    // init now parks on it (model build overlaps camera acquisition), so
+    // the harness must deliver it or init never reaches calibration_read.
+    send({ type: "camera_geometry", width: 640, height: 480, resolutionName: "640x480" });
+    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(workerMessages.some((m) => m.type === "calibration_read")).toBe(true));
+    const readRequest = workerMessages.find((m) => m.type === "calibration_read") as { id: number };
+    send({ type: "calibration_read_result", id: readRequest.id, response: { ok: true, text: null } });
+    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(workerMessages.some((m) => m.type === "backend")).toBe(true));
+    workerMessages.length = 0;
+    return send;
+  }
+
+  async function sendFrame(send: (message: unknown) => void): Promise<void> {
+    const done = workerMessages.filter((m) => m.type === "frame_done").length;
+    send({
+      type: "frame",
+      data: new Uint8ClampedArray(4 * 640 * 480),
+      width: 640,
+      height: 480,
+      captureMs: 1,
+      capturedAt: performance.now(),
+      droppedFrames: 0,
+      mainThreadLongTasks: 0
+    });
+    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(workerMessages.filter((m) => m.type === "frame_done").length).toBeGreaterThan(done));
+  }
+
+  function gazePayloads(): Array<Record<string, unknown>> {
+    return workerMessages
+      .filter((m) => m.type === "backend")
+      .map((m) => (m as { payload: Record<string, unknown> }).payload)
+      .filter((payload) => payload.type === "gaze");
+  }
+
+  function statusPayloads(): Array<Record<string, unknown>> {
+    return workerMessages
+      .filter((m) => m.type === "backend")
+      .map((m) => (m as { payload: Record<string, unknown> }).payload)
+      .filter((payload) => payload.type === "status");
+  }
+
+  // sendFrame() polls with real timers — during a fake-timers recovery the
+  // frame must be sent raw and clock advanced manually.
+  function sendRawFrame(send: (message: unknown) => void): void {
+    send({
+      type: "frame",
+      data: new Uint8ClampedArray(4 * 640 * 480),
+      width: 640,
+      height: 480,
+      captureMs: 1,
+      capturedAt: performance.now(),
+      droppedFrames: 0,
+      mainThreadLongTasks: 0
+    });
+  }
+
+  it("set_paused drops frames without emitting and unpause resumes cleanly", async () => {
+    const send = await startWorker();
+    await sendFrame(send);
+    expect(gazePayloads().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    workerMessages.length = 0;
+    send({ type: "set_paused", paused: true });
+    await sendFrame(send);
+    await sendFrame(send);
+    // Paused frames still post frame_done (the pump handshake) but never a
+    // backend payload — no gaze, no status spam.
+    expect(workerMessages.filter((m) => m.type === "backend")).toHaveLength(0);
+    workerMessages.length = 0;
+    send({ type: "set_paused", paused: false });
+    await sendFrame(send);
+    expect(gazePayloads().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("no-face frames emit a ~1Hz away heartbeat — liveness, never a sample", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker();
+      // Every detect comes back empty — the boot-away case: lastEmitCore is
+      // null, so heartbeats start immediately rather than after 8s.
+      workerModelsControl.detectResult = { head: null, eyes: [], mouth: null };
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      const beats = gazePayloads();
+      // ~1Hz: four frames over ~3.3s yield 3-4 beats, and the cadence gate
+      // means the second frame in the same second can't double-emit.
+      expect(beats.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
+      expect(beats.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(4);
+      for (const beat of beats) {
+        expect(beat.away).toBe(true);
+        expect(beat.held_reason).toBe("no_face");
+        // Liveness only — no coordinates a consumer could read as a gaze.
+        expect(beat.x_norm).toBeUndefined();
+        expect(beat.y_norm).toBeUndefined();
+      }
+      // A face returning clears the marker on the very next valid emit.
+      workerModelsControl.detectResult = null;
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      const tail = gazePayloads().slice(beats.length);
+      expect(tail.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+      expect(tail.every((p) => p.away === undefined && typeof p.x_norm === "number")).toBe(true);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectResult = null;
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("filter_options dwellLock toggles anchoring while frames keep flowing", async () => {
+    const send = await startWorker();
+    send({ type: "filter_options", dwellLock: false });
+    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) {
+      await sendFrame(send);
+    }
+    // Static fixation that dwell-locks by default — anchoring never engages
+    // while disabled, but filtered gaze still emits every frame.
+    expect(gazePayloads().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    expect(gazePayloads().some((p) => p.gaze_state === "dwell")).toBe(false);
+    send({ type: "filter_options", dwellLock: true });
+    let locked = false;
+    for (let i = 0; i < 12 && !locked; i += 1) {
+      await sendFrame(send);
+      locked = gazePayloads().some((p) => p.gaze_state === "dwell");
+    }
+    expect(locked).toBe(true);
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("rebuilds a lost wasm session after backoff instead of erroring every frame", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker();
+      // Detector only runs once searchInterval/DETECT_INTERVAL_MS has
+      // elapsed on the fake clock — advance past both so frames hit it.
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send); // healthy frame → lastDetection primed
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("cannot run inference. invalid session id: 12726032");
+      sendRawFrame(send); // detect throws → session-lost recovery
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(3000);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      const statuses = statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message));
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m.includes("rebuilding sessions"))).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m === "Models reloaded with wasm")).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m.includes("inference unrecoverable"))).toBe(false);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      // Post-recovery frames produce gaze again on the rebuilt session.
+      workerMessages.length = 0;
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      expect(gazePayloads().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("counts a rebuilt session that fails its probe run as a failed attempt", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker();
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("cannot run inference. invalid session id: 5");
+      // First rebuilt session creates cleanly but can't run — must not be
+      // declared recovered; attempt 2 succeeds and tracking resumes.
+      workerModelsControl.warmupFailures = 1;
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(3000);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(6000);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      const statuses = statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message));
+      expect(statuses.filter((m) => m.includes("rebuilding sessions"))).toHaveLength(2);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m === "Models reloaded with wasm")).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m.includes("inference unrecoverable"))).toBe(false);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerModelsControl.warmupFailures = 0;
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("emits one unrecoverable status after rebuild attempts run out, then goes quiet", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker();
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("cannot run inference. invalid session id: 9");
+      workerModelsControl.createError = new Error("memory access out of bounds");
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      // 3s + 6s + 12s of backoff, then terminal.
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(30000);
+      const statuses = statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message));
+      expect(statuses.filter((m) => m.includes("inference unrecoverable — restart tracking"))).toHaveLength(1);
+      // Terminal: later frames still ack via frame_done but emit nothing —
+      // the dead-session spam that wedged the old loop is gone.
+      workerMessages.length = 0;
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      expect(workerMessages.filter((m) => m.type === "backend")).toHaveLength(0);
+      expect(workerMessages.some((m) => m.type === "frame_done")).toBe(true);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerModelsControl.createError = null;
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("rebuilds webgpu in place on the short ladder before any wasm demotion", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker("webgpu");
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send); // healthy frame on webgpu — lastDetection primed
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      // Dawn-style device loss mid-run: recoverable, and the fast path is
+      // retried first — the tracker must prefer webgpu ALWAYS.
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("AbortError: the GPU device is lost");
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1500);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      const statuses = statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message));
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m.includes("rebuilding webgpu sessions"))).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m === "Models reloaded with webgpu")).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m.includes("inference unrecoverable"))).toBe(false);
+      // Init + one recovery rung, both webgpu — wasm was never touched.
+      expect(workerModelsControl.createCalls).toEqual(["webgpu", "webgpu"]);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("demotes to wasm only after the webgpu ladder exhausts, then quietly re-promotes", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker("webgpu");
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("ORT_ENFORCE failed in MapAsync callback");
+      workerModelsControl.createErrorFor.webgpu = new Error("webgpu device unavailable");
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      // webgpu rungs (1.5s + 5s) both fail, then wasm rung 1 lands at +3s.
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1500 + 5000 + 3000 + 100);
+      const statuses = statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message));
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m.includes("webgpu session rebuilds exhausted"))).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m === "Models reloaded with wasm")).toBe(true);
+      expect(workerModelsControl.createCalls).toEqual(["webgpu", "webgpu", "webgpu", "wasm"]);
+      // wasm is never a permanent silent downgrade: the landing armed a
+      // quiet re-promotion probe at +60s.
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerModelsControl.createErrorFor = {};
+      workerMessages.length = 0;
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(60000);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(2500); // let the swapped-set dispose drain
+      expect(workerModelsControl.createCalls.at(-1)).toBe("webgpu");
+      const laterStatuses = statusPayloads();
+      expect(laterStatuses.some((p) => p.message === "Models reloaded with webgpu")).toBe(true);
+      // Quiet promotion: the only emitted status is the info-level reload —
+      // no warning/error feeds the host a false wedge signature.
+      expect(laterStatuses.every((p) => p.level === "info")).toBe(true);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerModelsControl.createErrorFor = {};
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("stays on wasm silently when the re-promotion probe declines", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker("webgpu");
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("invalid session id: 77");
+      // webgpu keeps failing — the tracker lands on wasm and stays there,
+      // retrying quietly on the ~5min cadence without spamming statuses.
+      workerModelsControl.createErrorFor.webgpu = new Error("webgpu still unavailable");
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1500 + 5000 + 3000 + 100);
+      expect(statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message)).some((m) => m === "Models reloaded with wasm")).toBe(true);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerMessages.length = 0;
+      // First probe at +60s fails quietly; next is scheduled at +5min.
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(60000 + 100);
+      expect(statusPayloads()).toHaveLength(0);
+      const createsAfterProbe = workerModelsControl.createCalls.length;
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300000);
+      // Second quiet attempt fired — still no host-visible statuses.
+      expect(workerModelsControl.createCalls.length).toBeGreaterThan(createsAfterProbe);
+      expect(statusPayloads()).toHaveLength(0);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerModelsControl.createErrorFor = {};
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("bounds a wedged session dispose so recovery still proceeds", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker("wasm");
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1100);
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = new Error("cannot run inference. invalid session id: 42");
+      // ORT 1.26 could wedge release() forever inside a Dawn callback — the
+      // 5s dispose timeout must unstick the ladder instead of ending the run.
+      workerModelsControl.disposeHang = true;
+      const warnSpy = vi.spyOn(console, "warn");
+      sendRawFrame(send);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(5000 + 3000 + 100);
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      const statuses = statusPayloads().map((p) => String(p.message));
+      // The dispose failure is console-only telemetry; the recovery ladder
+      // proceeding past the hung release is what must be host-visible.
+      expect(warnSpy.mock.calls.some((call) => String(call[0]).includes("dispose failed"))).toBe(true);
+      expect(statuses.some((m) => m === "Models reloaded with wasm")).toBe(true);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectError = null;
+      workerModelsControl.disposeHang = false;
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+
+  it("serializes frame processing — a second frame is dropped+acked, never overlapped", async () => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+    let releaseGate: (() => void) | undefined;
+    try {
+      const send = await startWorker("wasm");
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300);
+      workerModelsControl.detectGate = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
+        releaseGate = resolve;
+      });
+      sendRawFrame(send); // parks inside detect on the gate
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      expect(workerModelsControl.detectCalls).toBe(1);
+      sendRawFrame(send); // mid-flight: in-flight guard drops it but acks —
+      // the pump's dropped-frame contract is preserved.
+      expect(workerMessages.filter((m) => m.type === "frame_done")).toHaveLength(1);
+      // Frame 2 never reached detect — no overlapping calls on shared state.
+      expect(workerModelsControl.detectCalls).toBe(1);
+      // A control message doesn't queue behind the parked frame — stop lands
+      // immediately (no stop() deadlock while inference is mid-flight).
+      send({ type: "stop" });
+      workerModelsControl.detectGate = null;
+      releaseGate?.();
+      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
+      expect(workerMessages.filter((m) => m.type === "frame_done")).toHaveLength(2);
+      expect(workerModelsControl.maxDetectInFlight).toBe(1);
+    } finally {
+      workerModelsControl.detectGate = null;
+      releaseGate?.();
+      // stop left the module stopped; a fresh init in the next test resets it.
+      vi.useRealTimers();
+    }
+    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  });
+});
+
+// The model-input samplers were rewritten to scalar bilinear reads (the old
+// path allocated ~5 arrays per output pixel). These reference builders keep
+// the ORIGINAL per-pixel math so the optimized output can be proven
+// bit-identical rather than approximately-equal.
+describe("scalar bilinear input sampling", () => {
+  function refPixel(data: Uint8ClampedArray, width: number, x: number, y: number): [number, number, number] {
+    const offset = (y * width + x) * 4;
+    return [data[offset], data[offset + 1], data[offset + 2]];
+  }
+
+  function refSampleRgb(data: Uint8ClampedArray, width: number, height: number, x: number, y: number): [number, number, number] {
+    if (x < 0 || y < 0 || x > width - 1 || y > height - 1) {
+      return [0, 0, 0];
+    }
+    const x0 = Math.floor(x);
+    const y0 = Math.floor(y);
+    const x1 = Math.min(width - 1, x0 + 1);
+    const y1 = Math.min(height - 1, y0 + 1);
+    const wx = x - x0;
+    const wy = y - y0;
+    const c00 = refPixel(data, width, x0, y0);
+    const c10 = refPixel(data, width, x1, y0);
+    const c01 = refPixel(data, width, x0, y1);
+    const c11 = refPixel(data, width, x1, y1);
+    return [0, 1, 2].map((channel) => {
+      const top = c00[channel] * (1 - wx) + c10[channel] * wx;
+      const bottom = c01[channel] * (1 - wx) + c11[channel] * wx;
+      return top * (1 - wy) + bottom * wy;
+    }) as [number, number, number];
+  }
+
+  // A noisy fixture with the head box pushed off-frame so both the in-frame
+  // bilinear taps and the out-of-frame neutral path get exercised.
+  function fixtureFrame(width: number, height: number): { data: Uint8ClampedArray; width: number; height: number } {
+    const data = new Uint8ClampedArray(width * height * 4);
+    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i += 1) {
+      data[i] = (i * 37 + 11) % 256;
+    }
+    return { data, width, height };
+  }
+
+  function firstMismatch(actual: ArrayLike<number>, expected: ArrayLike<number>): number {
+    for (let i = 0; i < expected.length; i += 1) {
+      if (!Object.is(actual[i], expected[i])) {
+        return i;
+      }
+    }
+    return -1;
+  }
+
+  it("createGazeInput is bit-identical to the naive per-pixel path", () => {
+    const frame = fixtureFrame(96, 64);
+    // Head hangs off the left/top edge so some source taps sample out-of-frame.
+    const head = { classId: 7, score: 1, x1: -10, y1: -8, x2: 60, y2: 50 };
+    const eyes = [
+      { classId: 17, score: 1, x1: 2, y1: 10, x2: 14, y2: 18 },
+      { classId: 17, score: 1, x1: 30, y1: 10, x2: 42, y2: 18 }
+    ];
+    const crop = createGazeInput(frame as ImageData, head, eyes);
+
+    const left: [number, number] = [(eyes[0].x1 + eyes[0].x2) * 0.5, (eyes[0].y1 + eyes[0].y2) * 0.5];
+    const right: [number, number] = [(eyes[1].x1 + eyes[1].x2) * 0.5, (eyes[1].y1 + eyes[1].y2) * 0.5];
+    const eyeCenter: [number, number] = [(left[0] + right[0]) * 0.5, (left[1] + right[1]) * 0.5];
+    const eyeDistance = Math.hypot(right[0] - left[0], right[1] - left[1]);
+    const cropSize = Math.max((head.x2 - head.x1) / 1.5, eyeDistance) * 1.5;
+    const scale = GAZE_INPUT_SIZE / Math.max(1, cropSize);
+    const inverseScale = 1 / scale;
+    const inverseTx = eyeCenter[0] - GAZE_INPUT_SIZE * 0.5 * inverseScale;
+    const inverseTy = eyeCenter[1] - GAZE_INPUT_SIZE * 0.5 * inverseScale;
+    const plane = GAZE_INPUT_SIZE * GAZE_INPUT_SIZE;
+    const reference = new Float32Array(3 * plane);
+    for (let y = 0; y < GAZE_INPUT_SIZE; y += 1) {
+      for (let x = 0; x < GAZE_INPUT_SIZE; x += 1) {
+        const [r, g, b] = refSampleRgb(frame.data, frame.width, frame.height, x * inverseScale + inverseTx, y * inverseScale + inverseTy);
+        const dst = y * GAZE_INPUT_SIZE + x;
+        reference[dst] = r / 127.5 - 1;
+        reference[plane + dst] = g / 127.5 - 1;
+        reference[plane * 2 + dst] = b / 127.5 - 1;
+      }
+    }
+    expect(firstMismatch(crop.input, reference)).toBe(-1);
+    // The geometry outputs are the un-sampled part of the contract.
+    expect(crop.inverseScale).toBe(inverseScale);
+    expect(crop.inverseTx).toBe(inverseTx);
+    expect(crop.inverseTy).toBe(inverseTy);
+  });
+
+  it("createAppearanceInput is bit-identical to the naive per-pixel path", () => {
+    const frame = fixtureFrame(120, 80);
+    const head = { classId: 7, score: 1, x1: -20, y1: 4, x2: 90, y2: 70 };
+    const actual = createAppearanceInput(frame as ImageData, head);
+
+    const mean = [0.485, 0.456, 0.406];
+    const std = [0.229, 0.224, 0.225];
+    const headCx = (head.x1 + head.x2) * 0.5;
+    const headCy = (head.y1 + head.y2) * 0.5;
+    const side = Math.max(head.x2 - head.x1, head.y2 - head.y1) * 1.5;
+    const scale = APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE / Math.max(1, side);
+    const inverseScale = 1 / scale;
+    const inverseTx = headCx - APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE * 0.5 * inverseScale;
+    const inverseTy = headCy - APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE * 0.5 * inverseScale;
+    const plane = APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE * APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE;
+    const reference = new Float32Array(3 * plane);
+    for (let y = 0; y < APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE; y += 1) {
+      for (let x = 0; x < APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE; x += 1) {
+        const [r, g, b] = refSampleRgb(frame.data, frame.width, frame.height, x * inverseScale + inverseTx, y * inverseScale + inverseTy);
+        const dst = y * APPEARANCE_INPUT_SIZE + x;
+        reference[dst] = (r / 255 - mean[0]) / std[0];
+        reference[plane + dst] = (g / 255 - mean[1]) / std[1];
+        reference[plane * 2 + dst] = (b / 255 - mean[2]) / std[2];
+      }
+    }
+    expect(firstMismatch(actual, reference)).toBe(-1);
+  });
+});

+export function isRecoverableInferenceError(error: unknown): boolean {
+  // Case-insensitive: ORT/Dawn error strings vary in casing across versions
+  // (AbortError vs aborterror, MapAsync vs mapAsync).
+  const message = (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)).toLowerCase();
+  const name = error instanceof Error ? error.name.toLowerCase() : "";
+  return (
+    message.includes("ortrun") ||
+    // A run against a released/dead session — only a rebuild can fix it.
+    message.includes("invalid session id") ||
+    message.includes("bad_array_new_length") ||
+    message.includes("failed to call") ||
+    message.includes("memory access out of bounds") ||
+    message.includes("error_code") ||
+    // Dawn/WebGPU device-loss signatures — device loss can still surface
+    // mid-run on real GPUs; these must start the (webgpu-first) ladder,
+    // not spam frames.
+    message.includes("device is lost") ||
+    message.includes("device lost") ||
+    message.includes("instance reference") ||
+    message.includes("mapasync") ||
+    message.includes("aborterror") ||
+    name === "aborterror"
+  );

+// Verify-sweep outcome for a pending fit: normalized-screen error statistics
+// plus medians bucketed by target region, so corner/edge regressions surface
+// instead of being averaged into one number.
+export interface VerifyVerdict {
+  median: number;
+  p90: number;
+  max: number;
+  samples: number;
+  regions: {
+    center?: number;
+    edge?: number;
+    corner?: number;
+  };
+}
+
+export function regionOfTarget(target: [number, number]): "center" | "edge" | "corner" {
+  const dx = Math.abs(target[0] - 0.5);
+  const dy = Math.abs(target[1] - 0.5);
+  if (Math.hypot(dx, dy) < 0.2) return "center";
+  // True corners only: an edge midpoint is far on ONE axis and centred on the
+  // other — the old radial check mislabeled those as corners.
+  return dx > 0.35 && dy > 0.35 ? "corner" : "edge";
+}
+
+function medianOf(values: number[]): number | undefined {
+  if (values.length === 0) return undefined;
+  const sorted = values.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
+  return sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)];
+}
+
+export function buildVerifyVerdict(validation: Array<{ target: [number, number]; error: number }>): VerifyVerdict | null {
+  if (validation.length === 0) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  const errors = validation.map((v) => v.error).sort((a, b) => a - b);
+  const regions: VerifyVerdict["regions"] = {};
+  for (const region of ["center", "edge", "corner"] as const) {
+    const bucket = validation.filter((v) => regionOfTarget(v.target) === region).map((v) => v.error);
+    const median = medianOf(bucket);
+    if (median !== undefined) {
+      regions[region] = Number(median.toFixed(4));
+    }
+  }
+  return {
+    median: errors[Math.floor(errors.length / 2)],
+    p90: errors[Math.floor(errors.length * 0.9)],
+    max: errors[errors.length - 1],
+    samples: errors.length,
+    regions
+  };
 }

+// Scalar bilinear read of one RGB channel. The old path allocated ~5 arrays
+// per pixel ([r,g,b] + four pixel() tuples + the map() result); at the
+// 160²/448² targets that was ~2.4M allocs/s of pure GC churn. This keeps the
+// SAME arithmetic — per-channel top/bottom lerp in the original operand
+// order — so tensor output is bit-identical with zero allocations. Callers

+function bilinearChannel(
+  data: Uint8ClampedArray,
+  i00: number,
+  i10: number,
+  i01: number,
+  i11: number,
+  wx: number,
+  wy: number,
+  channel: number
+): number {
+  const top = data[i00 + channel] * (1 - wx) + data[i10 + channel] * wx;
+  const bottom = data[i01 + channel] * (1 - wx) + data[i11 + channel] * wx;
+  return top * (1 - wy) + bottom * wy;

+// Rate-limits the (relatively expensive) appearance pass and EMA-smooths its
+// output so the feature vector sees a stable signal instead of per-run jitter.
+// Inference is fired without awaiting — on a threaded ORT wasm build the
+// compute happens on ORT's own workers and the frame loop stays responsive.
+export class AppearanceChannel {
+  private pending = false;
+  private pendingSince = -Infinity;
+  private lastRunAt = -Infinity;
+  private lastDurationMs = 0;
+  private smoothed: (AppearanceAngles & { at: number }) | null = null;
+  private failures = 0;
+
+  constructor(
+    private readonly periodMs: number = APPEARANCE_PERIOD_MS,
+    private readonly ema: number = 0.45,
+    private readonly staleMs: number = APPEARANCE_STALE_MS
+  ) {}
+
+  get disabled(): boolean {
+    return this.failures >= 3;
+  }
+
+  maybeRun(now: number, estimate: () => Promise<AppearanceAngles>): void {
+    // Adaptive duty cycle: the effective period is max(periodMs, 4× last
+    // inference duration) so the model can never exceed ~25% of wall time —
+    // on a single-threaded ORT build (no crossOriginIsolation, e.g. packaged
+    // file:// loads) a ~90ms call backs off to ~3fps instead of hitching.
+    const effectivePeriod = Math.max(this.periodMs, this.lastDurationMs * 4);
+    if (this.pending) {
+      // A promise that never settles (hung wasm session) would wedge the
+      // channel forever — clear the lock once it's older than any plausible
+      // inference. The late resolve still lands harmlessly.
+      if (now - this.pendingSince > APPEARANCE_PENDING_STALE_MS) {
+        this.pending = false;
+      } else {
+        return;
+      }
+    }
+    if (this.disabled || now - this.lastRunAt < effectivePeriod) {
+      return;
+    }
+    this.pending = true;
+    this.pendingSince = now;
+    this.lastRunAt = now;
+    const runStart = performance.now();
+    let result: Promise<AppearanceAngles>;
+    try {
+      result = estimate();
+    } catch {
+      // A synchronous throw never reaches .finally — clear pending here or
+      // the channel stays wedged.
+      this.pending = false;
+      this.failures += 1;
+      return;
+    }
+    result
+      .then((angles) => {
+        this.lastDurationMs = performance.now() - runStart;
+        // Reject non-finite output rather than poisoning the EMA — one NaN
+        // frame would otherwise stick in `smoothed` permanently.
+        if (angles === null || ![angles.yawDeg, angles.pitchDeg, angles.confidence].every(Number.isFinite)) {
+          this.failures += 1;
+          return;
+        }
+        const prev = this.smoothed;
+        this.smoothed = prev
+          ? {
+              yawDeg: prev.yawDeg + (angles.yawDeg - prev.yawDeg) * this.ema,
+              pitchDeg: prev.pitchDeg + (angles.pitchDeg - prev.pitchDeg) * this.ema,
+              confidence: prev.confidence + (angles.confidence - prev.confidence) * this.ema,
+              at: now
+            }
+          : { ...angles, at: now };
+      })
+      .catch(() => {
+        this.failures += 1;
+      })
+      .finally(() => {
+        this.pending = false;
+      });
   }
-  const x0 = Math.floor(x);
-  const y0 = Math.floor(y);
-  const x1 = Math.min(frame.width - 1, x0 + 1);

+    out[k * 3 + 1] = points[src];
+    out[k * 3 + 2] = points[src + 2];
+  }
+  return out;
+}
+
+// Applies the documented rotation convention R = Rz(roll)·Ry(-yaw)·Rx(pitch)
+// to a k×3 point set — the inverse of what the estimator extracts, so tests
+// build "known pose" meshes through exactly the semantics the fit recovers.
+export function applyPoseRotation(points: Float32Array, yawDeg: number, pitchDeg: number, rollDeg: number): Float32Array {
+  const yaw = (yawDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
+  const pitch = (pitchDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
+  const roll = (rollDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
+  const cy = Math.cos(yaw);
+  const sy = Math.sin(yaw);
+  const cp = Math.cos(pitch);
+  const sp = Math.sin(pitch);
+  const cr = Math.cos(roll);
+  const sr = Math.sin(roll);
+  const r00 = cr * cy;
+  const r01 = -cr * sy * sp - sr * cp;
+  const r02 = -cr * sy * cp + sr * sp;
+  const r10 = sr * cy;
+  const r11 = -sr * sy * sp + cr * cp;
+  const r12 = -sr * sy * cp - cr * sp;
+  const r20 = sy;
+  const r21 = cy * sp;
+  const r22 = cy * cp;
+  const out = new Float32Array(points.length);
+  for (let i = 0; i + 2 < points.length; i += 3) {
+    const x = points[i];
+    const y = points[i + 1];
+    const z = points[i + 2];
+    out[i] = r00 * x + r01 * y + r02 * z;
+    out[i + 1] = r10 * x + r11 * y + r12 * z;
+    out[i + 2] = r20 * x + r21 * y + r22 * z;
+  }
+  return out;
+}
+
+interface PoseFit {
+  rotation: number[][];
+  refCenter: [number, number, number];
+  liveCenter: [number, number, number];
+}
+
+// Rigid Kabsch alignment (Horn's quaternion form): the rotation R with
+// live ≈ s·R·ref + t — scale and translation are absorbed, so the recovered
+// rotation is distance- and framing-invariant. Degenerate clouds (collapsed
+// depth, constant points, any non-finite coordinate) return null so callers
+// fall back to the detector proxies instead of emitting NaN pose.
+function fitPoseRotation(reference: Float32Array, live: Float32Array): PoseFit | null {
+  if (reference.length !== live.length || live.length < 9 || live.length % 3 !== 0) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  const n = live.length / 3;
+  const refCenter: [number, number, number] = [0, 0, 0];
+  const liveCenter: [number, number, number] = [0, 0, 0];
+  for (let i = 0; i < live.length; i += 3) {
+    refCenter[0] += reference[i];
+    refCenter[1] += reference[i + 1];
+    refCenter[2] += reference[i + 2];
+    liveCenter[0] += live[i];
+    liveCenter[1] += live[i + 1];
+    liveCenter[2] += live[i + 2];
+  }
+  for (let axis = 0; axis < 3; axis += 1) {
+    refCenter[axis] /= n;
+    liveCenter[axis] /= n;
+  }
+  let sxx = 0;
+  let sxy = 0;
+  let sxz = 0;
+  let syx = 0;
+  let syy = 0;
+  let syz = 0;
+  let szx = 0;
+  let szy = 0;
+  let szz = 0;
+  let refVar = 0;
+  let liveVar = 0;
+  for (let i = 0; i < live.length; i += 3) {
+    const ax = reference[i] - refCenter[0];
+    const ay = reference[i + 1] - refCenter[1];
+    const az = reference[i + 2] - refCenter[2];
+    const bx = live[i] - liveCenter[0];
+    const by = live[i + 1] - liveCenter[1];
+    const bz = live[i + 2] - liveCenter[2];
+    if (![ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz].every(Number.isFinite)) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    sxx += ax * bx;
+    sxy += ax * by;
+    sxz += ax * bz;
+    syx += ay * bx;
+    syy += ay * by;
+    syz += ay * bz;
+    szx += az * bx;
+    szy += az * by;
+    szz += az * bz;
+    refVar += ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az;
+    liveVar += bx * bx + by * by + bz * bz;
+  }
+  if (!Number.isFinite(refVar) || !Number.isFinite(liveVar) || refVar < 1e-6 || liveVar < 1e-6) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  const trace = sxx + syy + szz;
+  const nMat = [
+    [trace, syz - szy, szx - sxz, sxy - syx],
+    [syz - szy, sxx - syy - szz, sxy + syx, szx + sxz],
+    [szx - sxz, sxy + syx, -sxx + syy - szz, syz + szy],
+    [sxy - syx, szx + sxz, syz + szy, -sxx - syy + szz]
+  ];
+  // Gershgorin shift makes the matrix PSD, so power iteration lands on the
+  // TOP eigenvector — the least-squares rotation quaternion — rather than
+  // whichever eigenvalue happens to be largest in magnitude.
+  let shift = 0;
+  for (let r = 0; r < 4; r += 1) {
+    let radius = 0;
+    for (let c = 0; c < 4; c += 1) {
+      radius += Math.abs(nMat[r][c]);
+    }
+    if (radius > shift) {
+      shift = radius;
+    }
+  }
+  for (let r = 0; r < 4; r += 1) {
+    nMat[r][r] += shift;
+  }
+  let q: [number, number, number, number] = [1, 0, 0, 0];
+  for (let iter = 0; iter < 48; iter += 1) {
+    const w0 = nMat[0][0] * q[0] + nMat[0][1] * q[1] + nMat[0][2] * q[2] + nMat[0][3] * q[3];
+    const w1 = nMat[1][0] * q[0] + nMat[1][1] * q[1] + nMat[1][2] * q[2] + nMat[1][3] * q[3];
+    const w2 = nMat[2][0] * q[0] + nMat[2][1] * q[1] + nMat[2][2] * q[2] + nMat[2][3] * q[3];
+    const w3 = nMat[3][0] * q[0] + nMat[3][1] * q[1] + nMat[3][2] * q[2] + nMat[3][3] * q[3];
+    const norm = Math.hypot(w0, w1, w2, w3);
+    if (!Number.isFinite(norm) || norm < 1e-12) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    q = [w0 / norm, w1 / norm, w2 / norm, w3 / norm];
+  }
+  const [qw, qx, qy, qz] = q;
+  const rotation = [
+    [1 - 2 * (qy * qy + qz * qz), 2 * (qx * qy - qw * qz), 2 * (qx * qz + qw * qy)],
+    [2 * (qx * qy + qw * qz), 1 - 2 * (qx * qx + qz * qz), 2 * (qy * qz - qw * qx)],
+    [2 * (qx * qz - qw * qy), 2 * (qy * qz + qw * qx), 1 - 2 * (qx * qx + qy * qy)]
+  ];
+  return { rotation, refCenter, liveCenter };
+}
+
+function headPoseFromRotation(r: number[][]): HeadPose | null {
+  const yawDeg = (Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, r[2][0]))) * 180) / Math.PI;
+  const pitchDeg = (Math.atan2(r[2][1], r[2][2]) * 180) / Math.PI;
+  const rollDeg = (Math.atan2(r[1][0], r[0][0]) * 180) / Math.PI;
+  if (![yawDeg, pitchDeg, rollDeg].every(Number.isFinite)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  return { yawDeg, pitchDeg, rollDeg };
+}
+
+// Head rotation of `live` (a headPosePoints subset) against `reference` in
+// the same subset layout — the pure fit; HeadPoseBaseline owns which cloud
+// serves as the reference.
+export function estimateHeadPoseFromMesh(live: Float32Array, reference: Float32Array): HeadPose | null {
+  const fit = fitPoseRotation(reference, live);
+  if (fit === null) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  return headPoseFromRotation(fit.rotation);
+}
+
+// Session "straight-ahead" the live mesh is compared against: the user's own
+// neutral pose, not an anatomical template, so per-face geometry differences
+// cancel instead of biasing the angles. The first valid mesh alone can catch
+// a mid-turn or a half-settled frame — the seed is instead the per-vertex
+// median of the first few NEAR-NEUTRAL meshes (a held turn outside the
+// adapt band never enters the pool). After seeding, the reference EMA-adapts
+// ONLY while the pose already reads near-neutral — slow posture drift
+// converges into the zero, a held turn outside the band can't.
+export class HeadPoseBaseline {
+  private reference: Float32Array | null = null;
+  private seedPool: Float32Array[] = [];
+
+  constructor(
+    private readonly adaptAlpha = 0.005,
+    private readonly adaptLimitDeg = 10,
+    private readonly seedCount = 5
+  ) {}
+
+  get ready(): boolean {
+    return this.reference !== null;
+  }
+
+  // One headPosePoints subset per estimated frame; null on malformed or
+  // degenerate input — the proxy path is the caller's fallback.
+  update(live: Float32Array): HeadPose | null {
+    if (live.length % 3 !== 0 || live.length < 9) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    for (let i = 0; i < live.length; i += 1) {
+      if (!Number.isFinite(live[i])) {
+        return null;
+      }
+    }
+    if (this.reference === null) {
+      this.reference = live.slice();
+      this.seedPool = [live.slice()];
+      return { yawDeg: 0, pitchDeg: 0, rollDeg: 0 };
+    }
+    const fit = fitPoseRotation(this.reference, live);
+    if (fit === null) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    const pose = headPoseFromRotation(fit.rotation);
+    if (pose === null) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    if (Math.max(Math.abs(pose.yawDeg), Math.abs(pose.pitchDeg), Math.abs(pose.rollDeg)) <= this.adaptLimitDeg) {
+      if (this.seedPool.length < this.seedCount) {
+        // Still seeding: fold the near-neutral frame into the pool and move
+        // the reference to the running per-vertex median — an unlucky first
+        // mesh (mid-blink, mid-turn) is outvoted instead of owned forever.
+        this.seedPool.push(live.slice());
+        this.reference = medianPointCloud(this.seedPool);
+      } else {
+        this.adapt(fit, live);
+      }
+    }
+    return pose;
+  }
+
+  // Blend the fit-aligned live cloud into the reference — the user's
+  // habitual posture drifts slowly, so the neutral it measures against may
+  // too; near-neutral-only gating keeps a held turn from dragging the zero.
+  private adapt(fit: PoseFit, live: Float32Array): void {
+    const reference = this.reference as Float32Array;
+    const r = fit.rotation;
+    const [cx, cy, cz] = fit.liveCenter;
+    const [ox, oy, oz] = fit.refCenter;
+    const alpha = this.adaptAlpha;
+    for (let i = 0; i + 2 < reference.length; i += 3) {
+      const bx = live[i] - cx;
+      const by = live[i + 1] - cy;
+      const bz = live[i + 2] - cz;
+      const qx = r[0][0] * bx + r[1][0] * by + r[2][0] * bz + ox;
+      const qy = r[0][1] * bx + r[1][1] * by + r[2][1] * bz + oy;
+      const qz = r[0][2] * bx + r[1][2] * by + r[2][2] * bz + oz;
+      reference[i] += alpha * (qx - reference[i]);
+      reference[i + 1] += alpha * (qy - reference[i + 1]);
+      reference[i + 2] += alpha * (qz - reference[i + 2]);
+    }
+  }
+
+  reset(): void {
+    this.reference = null;
+    this.seedPool = [];
+  }
+}
+
+// Per-vertex positional median over a handful of same-layout clouds — the
+// median mesh is robust to one odd seed (blink warp, mid-turn frame) where
+// a mean would blend it in.
+function medianPointCloud(clouds: Float32Array[]): Float32Array {
+  const out = new Float32Array(clouds[0].length);
+  const column = new Array<number>(clouds.length);
+  for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i += 1) {
+    for (let k = 0; k < clouds.length; k += 1) {
+      column[k] = clouds[k][i];
+    }
+    column.sort((a, b) => a - b);
+    const mid = Math.floor(column.length / 2);
+    out[i] = column.length % 2 === 1 ? column[mid] : (column[mid - 1] + column[mid]) * 0.5;
+  }
+  return out;
+}

+    readonly heightPx: number,
+    readonly diagonalInch: number
+  ) {}

+  get sizeM(): [number, number] {
+    const diagonalM = this.diagonalInch * 0.0254;
+    const pixelDiagonal = Math.hypot(this.widthPx, this.heightPx);
+    return [(diagonalM * this.widthPx) / pixelDiagonal, (diagonalM * this.heightPx) / pixelDiagonal];
+  }

+// Residual-bias personalization (C4): a grid of bilinear-blended cell means
+// over the map's own residual errors — the per-user spatial bias the fitted
+// map leaves behind (e.g. the systematic pull one user's mesh shows at a
+// screen edge). Screen-normalized space like the affine chain: drops on a
+// context change, and per-cell shrinkage keeps sparse evidence from
+// overcorrecting. Fitting is O(n) binning — far under the in-browser budget.
+export interface ResidualBiasMap {
+  grid: number;
+  offsets: [number, number][];
+  counts: number[];
+}
+
+const RESIDUAL_BIAS_GRID = 4;
+// Cells need ~6 samples before their mean applies at full strength — a
+// single stray residual can't bend a region it barely visits.
+const RESIDUAL_BIAS_SHRINK = 6;
+const RESIDUAL_BIAS_MAX = 0.15;
+
+export function fitResidualBias(
+  points: [number, number][],
+  residuals: [number, number][],
+  grid = RESIDUAL_BIAS_GRID,
+  weights?: number[]
+): ResidualBiasMap | null {
+  if (points.length !== residuals.length || points.length < 12 || grid < 2 || (weights !== undefined && weights.length !== points.length)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  const cells = grid * grid;
+  const sums = Array.from({ length: cells }, () => [0, 0] as [number, number]);
+  const counts = new Array<number>(cells).fill(0);
+  for (let i = 0; i < points.length; i += 1) {
+    const [x, y] = points[i];
+    const [rx, ry] = residuals[i];
+    const w = weights === undefined ? 1 : weights[i];
+    if (![x, y, rx, ry, w].every(Number.isFinite) || w <= 0) {
+      continue;
+    }
+    const cx = Math.min(grid - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor(clamp01(x) * grid)));
+    const cy = Math.min(grid - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor(clamp01(y) * grid)));
+    const cell = cy * grid + cx;
+    sums[cell][0] += rx * w;
+    sums[cell][1] += ry * w;
+    counts[cell] += w;
+  }
+  const offsets: [number, number][] = [];
+  for (let c = 0; c < cells; c += 1) {
+    const count = counts[c];
+    if (count === 0) {
+      offsets.push([0, 0]);
+      continue;
+    }
+    const shrink = count / (count + RESIDUAL_BIAS_SHRINK);
+    let ox = (sums[c][0] / count) * shrink;
+    let oy = (sums[c][1] / count) * shrink;
+    const mag = Math.hypot(ox, oy);
+    if (mag > RESIDUAL_BIAS_MAX) {
+      ox *= RESIDUAL_BIAS_MAX / mag;
+      oy *= RESIDUAL_BIAS_MAX / mag;
+    }
+    offsets.push([ox, oy]);
+  }
+  return { grid, offsets, counts };
+}
+
+// Bilinear lookup of the residual field at a normalized-screen point — the
+// correction to ADD to a map output.
+export function residualBiasOffset(map: ResidualBiasMap, point: [number, number]): [number, number] {
+  const grid = map.grid;
+  const gx = clamp01(point[0]) * grid - 0.5;
+  const gy = clamp01(point[1]) * grid - 0.5;
+  const x0 = Math.min(grid - 2, Math.max(0, Math.floor(gx)));
+  const y0 = Math.min(grid - 2, Math.max(0, Math.floor(gy)));
+  const wx = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, gx - x0));
+  const wy = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, gy - y0));
+  let ox = 0;
+  let oy = 0;
+  for (const [cx, cy, w] of [
+    [x0, y0, (1 - wx) * (1 - wy)],
+    [x0 + 1, y0, wx * (1 - wy)],
+    [x0, y0 + 1, (1 - wx) * wy],
+    [x0 + 1, y0 + 1, wx * wy]
+  ] as const) {
+    const cell = map.offsets[cy * grid + cx];
+    ox += w * cell[0];
+    oy += w * cell[1];
+  }
+  return [ox, oy];
+}
