+  // Drift correction from the monitor's consistent-rejection vector.
+  // Each event applies at most DRIFT_MAX_STEP of screen — a nudge, never a
+  // teleport: a real reposition converges over successive sustained
+  // confirmations, while a bogus confirmation can't move the dot far enough
+  // to read as a jump. Returns the cumulative offset so callers can flag
+  // when it saturates — meaning something beyond a simple reposition is
+  // wrong.
+  applyDriftCorrection(dx: number, dy: number): [number, number] {
+    const step = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
+    if (!Number.isFinite(step) || step === 0) {
+      return this.outputOffset;
+    }
+    if (step > DRIFT_MAX_STEP) {
+      dx *= DRIFT_MAX_STEP / step;
+      dy *= DRIFT_MAX_STEP / step;
+    }
+    this.outputOffset[0] += dx;
+    this.outputOffset[1] += dy;
+    const mag = Math.hypot(this.outputOffset[0], this.outputOffset[1]);
+    if (mag > DRIFT_OFFSET_BOUND) {
+      this.outputOffset[0] *= DRIFT_OFFSET_BOUND / mag;
+      this.outputOffset[1] *= DRIFT_OFFSET_BOUND / mag;
+    }
+    this.evictStaleSamples();
+    this.persistOffset();
+    return this.outputOffset;
+  }

+  // geometry now misfit by ~the offset — dropping them stops the next refit
+  // from compromising between two camera poses. But the pool is calibration
+  // capital: keep at least the best ~40% (floor 24) so a marginal or wrong
+  // correction can never gut coverage in a single event — the persisted pool
+  // is written immediately after this runs.
+  private evictStaleSamples(): void {

+      return;

+      pair,
+      error: pointError(this.applyFeature(pair[0]), pair[1])

+    const floor = Math.max(24, Math.ceil(this.samples.length * 0.4));
+    const survivors = (keep.length >= floor ? keep : scored.slice(0, floor)).map((s) => s.pair);
+    const evicted = this.samples.length - survivors.length;
+    if (evicted > 0) {
+      this.samples.length = 0;

+  // Re-estimate how much correction is still needed from the freshest
+  // implicit evidence — call after a refit so the offset decays to zero as
+  // the map itself absorbs the new camera geometry.
+  private rehealDrift(): void {
+    if (this.implicitSamples.length < 8 || (this.outputOffset[0] === 0 && this.outputOffset[1] === 0)) {
+      return;
+    }
+    const residuals = this.implicitSamples.map(([feature, target]) => {
+      // Measure against what the user actually sees — the residual field's
+      // contribution must not be rehealed into the drift offset a second time.
+      const base = this.predictFeature(feature);
+      const [rx, ry] = this.residualAt(base);
+      return [target[0] - base[0] - rx, target[1] - base[1] - ry] as [number, number];
+    });

+    const my = medianOf(residuals.map((r) => r[1])) ?? 0;

+    let ty = my;

+    if (targetMag > DRIFT_OFFSET_BOUND) {
+      tx *= DRIFT_OFFSET_BOUND / targetMag;
+      ty *= DRIFT_OFFSET_BOUND / targetMag;

+  async refitWithImplicit(now: number): Promise<boolean> {
+    // Refit only when there's enough fresh evidence and enough time has passed;
+    // adopt only if the new map scores no worse than the current one. Either
+    // map kind can adapt — an affine-only calibration shouldn't freeze.
+    if ((this.featureMap === null && this.matrix === null) || this.implicitSamples.length < 30 || now - this.lastImplicitRefit < 90_000) {
+      return false;
+    }

+    // one target — the refit would only tighten a local screw, not heal the
+    // map. Require the fresh evidence to actually cover some screen.

+      let minY = 1;
+      let maxY = 0;
+      for (const [, target] of this.implicitSamples) {
+        minX = Math.min(minX, target[0]);
+        maxX = Math.max(maxX, target[0]);
+        minY = Math.min(minY, target[1]);
+        maxY = Math.max(maxY, target[1]);

+      if (Math.max(maxX - minX, maxY - minY) < 0.04) {

+// Greedy max-min subsample: the first point seeds it, each next pick is the
+// point farthest from everything already chosen — a coverage-preserving way
+// to thin a pool without biasing toward the newest or densest regions.
+function farthestPointSubset(points: [number, number][], k: number): [number, number][] {
+  if (points.length <= k) {
+    return points.slice();
+  }
+  const chosen = [points[0]];
+  const dist = points.map((p) => Math.hypot(p[0] - chosen[0][0], p[1] - chosen[0][1]));
+  while (chosen.length < k) {
+    let bestIdx = -1;
+    let bestDist = -1;
+    for (let i = 0; i < points.length; i += 1) {
+      if (dist[i] > bestDist) {
+        bestDist = dist[i];
+        bestIdx = i;
+      }
+    }
+    if (bestIdx < 0 || bestDist <= 0) {
+      break;
+    }
+    const picked = points[bestIdx];
+    chosen.push(picked);
+    dist[bestIdx] = -1;
+    for (let i = 0; i < points.length; i += 1) {
+      const d = Math.hypot(points[i][0] - picked[0], points[i][1] - picked[1]);
+      if (d < dist[i]) {
+        dist[i] = d;
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  return chosen;
+}
+
+// Same farthest-point walk returning indices — lets a tagged pool keep its
+// (feature, target) pairing while selection runs on the target geometry.
+function farthestPointIndices(points: [number, number][], k: number): number[] {
+  if (points.length <= k) {
+    return points.map((_, i) => i);

+export type EyeValidityState = "tracking" | "closing" | "closed";
+
+// Eye-openness as a state machine, not a flag (Soukupova–Čech EAR: blinks are
+// a temporal pattern, not a threshold). The corrupting frames are the
+// *transition* — the mesh mid-closure emits garbage before any confirmed-blink
+// flag could latch — so output holds the moment eyeOpen drops into the band,
+// before a blink is even confirmed.
+//
+//   tracking → closing  (eyeOpen < 0.55: hold immediately)
+//   closing  → closed   (2 consecutive frames < 0.28)
+//   closing  → tracking (recovers ≥0.6, or hovers mid-band >450ms — a squint
+//                        or talking posture, not a blink in progress)
+//   closed   → tracking (2 consecutive frames ≥0.6 — real reopen, not flicker;
+//                        or held >2.5s — occlusion/pathology, not a blink)
+export class EyeValidity {
+  private state: EyeValidityState = "tracking";
+  private closedStreak = 0;
+  private reopenStreak = 0;
+  private closingSince = 0;
+  private closedSince = 0;
+  private midBandSince = 0;
+  private settleUntil = 0;
+  private lastNow = 0;
+
+  update(eyeOpen: number, now: number): EyeValidityState {
+    this.lastNow = now;
+    if (!Number.isFinite(eyeOpen)) {
+      return this.state;
+    }
+    if (this.state === "tracking") {
+      if (eyeOpen < EYE_VALIDITY_ENTER) {
+        this.state = "closing";
+        this.closingSince = now;
+        this.closedStreak = 0;
+      }
+      return this.state;
+    }
+    if (this.state === "closing") {
+      if (eyeOpen < BLINK_CLOSE_THRESHOLD) {
+        this.closedStreak += 1;
+        if (this.closedStreak >= 2) {
+          this.state = "closed";
+          this.closedSince = now;
+          this.reopenStreak = 0;
+          this.midBandSince = 0;
+        }
+      } else if (eyeOpen >= EYE_VALIDITY_RECOVER || now - this.closingSince > CLOSING_TIMEOUT_MS) {
+        this.state = "tracking";
+        this.closedStreak = 0;
+        // A dip that never confirmed still passed mid-closure frames through —
+        // give the signal a beat to stabilize before emitting again.
+        this.settleUntil = now + 90;
+      }
+      return this.state;
+    }
+    // "closed": a real blink runs well under a second. A "blink" held past
+    // CLOSED_TIMEOUT_MS is occlusion or a pathological lid reading (squint,
+    // glare, hair over the eye), not a blink — release instead of freezing
+    // the output forever. If the signal still reads mid-band it re-enters
+    // closing on its own.
+    if (now - this.closedSince > CLOSED_TIMEOUT_MS) {
+      this.state = "tracking";
+      this.closedStreak = 0;
+      this.reopenStreak = 0;
+      this.midBandSince = 0;
+      return this.state;
+    }
+    // Squint trap: a mid-band reading (lid partially open) sustained ~1s is
+    // this user's open posture — ptosis, squint, glare — not a held blink.
+    // Reopen requires ≥0.6 which some users never produce; without this they
+    // park in "closed" until the 2.5s occlusion timeout on every blink.
+    if (eyeOpen >= BLINK_CLOSE_THRESHOLD && eyeOpen < EYE_VALIDITY_RECOVER) {
+      if (this.midBandSince === 0) {
+        this.midBandSince = now;
+      } else if (now - this.midBandSince >= SQUINT_RELEASE_MS) {
+        this.state = "tracking";
+        this.closedStreak = 0;
+        this.reopenStreak = 0;
+        this.midBandSince = 0;
+        this.settleUntil = now + 90;
+        return this.state;
+      }
+    } else {
+      this.midBandSince = 0;
+    }
+    if (eyeOpen >= EYE_VALIDITY_RECOVER) {
+      this.reopenStreak += 1;
+      if (this.reopenStreak >= 2) {
+        this.state = "tracking";
+        this.closedStreak = 0;
+        this.reopenStreak = 0;
+        // Reopen frames carry unstable angles (lid still recovering, iris
+        // contour half-occluded) — holding ~140ms is what stops the
+        // post-blink jump the user sees.
+        this.settleUntil = now + 140;
+      }
+    } else {
+      this.reopenStreak = 0;
+    }
+    return this.state;
+  }
+
+  get holding(): boolean {
+    return this.state !== "tracking" || this.lastNow < this.settleUntil;
+  }
+
+  get blinking(): boolean {
+    return this.state === "closed";
+  }
+
+  get current(): EyeValidityState {
+    return this.state;
+  }
+
+  reset(): void {
+    this.state = "tracking";
+    this.closedStreak = 0;
+    this.reopenStreak = 0;
+    this.closingSince = 0;
+    this.closedSince = 0;
+    this.midBandSince = 0;
+    this.settleUntil = 0;
+  }
 }

+// Constant-velocity coast during holds (the I-KF behaviour that beat I-VT on
+// ISO-9241 pointing evals): for the first ~400ms of a blink/loss the marker
+// eases along its last velocity instead of freezing mid-gesture; displacement
+// is capped so a stale velocity can't fly the dot away.
+export function coastPosition(
+  pos: [number, number],
+  vel: [number, number],
+  heldMs: number,
+  maxMs = 400,
+  maxStep = 0.045
+): [number, number] {
+  const t = Math.min(Math.max(heldMs, 0), maxMs) / 1000;
+  let dx = vel[0] * t;
+  let dy = vel[1] * t;
+  const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
+  if (d > maxStep) {
+    const s = maxStep / d;
+    dx *= s;
+    dy *= s;
+  }
+  return [clamp01(pos[0] + dx), clamp01(pos[1] + dy)];

+// the camera answers — the creates don't need capture dims. Resolves null
+// when a mid-build stop cut the fallback ladder short; the caller then knows
+// not to install the set.
+async function buildModelSet(
+  nextConfig: WebInferenceConfig,
+  previousModels: RuntimeModels | null
+): Promise<RuntimeModels | null> {
+  // A re-init must free the previous sessions before creating new ones —
+  // racing the old heap's async free is how a reload re-faults on the same
+  // OOM. The dispose is timeout-wrapped: a wedged release must not stall
+  // init forever.
+  await disposeRuntimeModels(previousModels, "previous session set");
+  // webgpu is opt-in only: "auto" resolves to wasm — the WebGPU EP wedges
+  // silently in InferenceSession.run() on Electron 42/macOS.
+  const preferredAccelerator: WebAccelerator = nextConfig.webAccelerator === "webgpu" ? "webgpu" : "wasm";
+  try {
+    return await withTimeout(createRuntimeModels(nextConfig, preferredAccelerator), MODEL_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS, "model create");
+  } catch (error) {
+    if (preferredAccelerator === "wasm") {
+      throw error;
+    }
+    const payload: BackendMessage = {
+      type: "status",
+      level: "warning",
+      message: `WebGPU model load failed in inference worker: ${error}; falling back to wasm`,

+      logged: true

+    // may still be tearing down asynchronously, and a same-beat wasm
+    // create can inherit the debris.
+    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => globalThis.setTimeout(resolve, 1000));

+      return null;
+    }

+      throw probeError;
+    }

+// value of ±1 means the iris touched the box edge. Falls back to [0,0] when
+// the mesh didn't localize the iris — the feature map treats it as neutral.
+function irisInBox(irisCenter: [number, number] | undefined, box: Detection): [number, number] {
+  if (irisCenter === undefined) {
+    return [0, 0];
+  }
+  const [cx, cy] = center(box);
+  const halfW = Math.max(4, width(box) * 0.5);
+  const halfH = Math.max(3, height(box) * 0.5);

+  const oy = Math.max(-1.5, Math.min(1.5, (irisCenter[1] - cy) / halfH));
+  return [ox, oy];

+// Bounds a single serialized session create: on the UB-wedged ORT 1.26
+// build (and any future Dawn-level wedge) a create can hang forever, which
+// used to stall the whole queue — every later rebuild then starved behind

+// ORT promise still settles on its own (its session is orphaned, nothing
+// references it, GC/bundle teardown reclaims it).

+export function withTimeout<T>(operation: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
+  let timer: ReturnType<typeof globalThis.setTimeout> | undefined;
+  const timeout = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
+    timer = globalThis.setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms}ms`)), ms);
+  });
+  return Promise.race([operation, timeout]).finally(() => {
+    if (timer !== undefined) {
+      globalThis.clearTimeout(timer);
     }
-  };
+  });

+// Away-mode liveness cadence — well inside the host's 6s stale window so
+// gaze.updated_at never lies about a live pipeline with no face in frame.
+const AWAY_HEARTBEAT_MS = 1000;
+
+// A released session frees its wasm heap asynchronously — a reload raced
+// against that free re-faults with the same OOM ("memory access out of
+// bounds"), which is how a recoverable crash became a permanent wedge.
+// The backoff gives each retry a genuinely clean heap; bounded, because a
+// permanently broken stack must not retry and log every frame forever.
+// Same ladder policy as the dedicated worker: wasm keeps the long backoff,
+// a transient webgpu device loss retries fast rather than costing 21s of
+// dead gaze, and wedged dispose/create calls are timeout-bounded.
+const SESSION_RECOVERY_DELAYS_MS = [3000, 6000, 12000];

+  // A dispose that can never hang the recovery path: on the wedged-release
+  // ORT bug the promise never settles, so after 5s the reference is dropped
+  // and the ladder moves on — its backoff absorbs the still-pending free.
+  const disposeRuntimeModels = async (target: RuntimeModels | null, context: string): Promise<void> => {
+    if (target === null) {
+      return;
+    }
+    try {
+      await withTimeout(target.dispose(), SESSION_DISPOSE_TIMEOUT_MS, "session dispose");
+    } catch (disposeError) {
+      logStatus(
+        {
+          type: "status",
+          level: "warning",
+          message: `${context} dispose failed`,
+          runtime: config.runtime,
+          accelerator: target.accelerator

+  // Rebuild the inference sessions in place after a session died — the same
+  // bounded-backoff recovery as the dedicated worker. Webgpu rungs use the
+  // short ladder (transient device loss shouldn't cost 21s of dead gaze);
+  // wasm keeps the long backoff so the heap actually frees between attempts.
+  // Each attempt then has to survive a real probe run — create succeeding
+  // while run faults counts as a failed attempt. Wasm exhaustion is terminal
+  // (emitted once, models stays null); webgpu exhaustion falls through to
+  // the wasm ladder. opts.promote keeps the live wasm set serving frames
+  // until a webgpu candidate passes its probe; opts.quiet keeps a declined
+  // probe log-only so the host never sees a false wedge signature.
+  const recoverSessions = async (target: WebAccelerator, cause: unknown, opts: { promote?: boolean; quiet?: boolean } = {}): Promise<boolean> => {
+    const quiet = opts.quiet === true;
+    const promote = opts.promote === true;
+    const preserved = promote ? models : null;
+    if (!promote) {
+      const dead = models;
+      models = null;
+      await disposeRuntimeModels(dead, "dead session");
+    }
+    const delays = target === "webgpu" ? WEBGPU_RECOVERY_DELAYS_MS : SESSION_RECOVERY_DELAYS_MS;
+    const attempts = promote ? 1 : delays.length;
+    let lastError: unknown = cause;
+    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < attempts; attempt += 1) {
+      const delayMs = promote ? 0 : delays[attempt];
+      const attemptPayload: BackendMessage = {
+        type: "status",
+        level: "warning",
+        message:
+          `${target} inference session lost: ${lastError instanceof Error ? lastError.message : String(lastError)}; ` +
+          `rebuilding sessions in ${delayMs / 1000}s (attempt ${attempt + 1}/${attempts})`,
+        runtime: config.runtime,
+        accelerator: target,
+        logged: true
+      };
+      logStatus(attemptPayload);
+      if (!quiet) {
+        emit(attemptPayload);
+      }
+      if (delayMs > 0) {
+        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => window.setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
+      }
+      if (stopped) {
+        return false;
+      }
+      try {
+        const rebuilt = await withTimeout(createRuntimeModels(config, target), MODEL_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS, "model create");
+        try {
+          await withTimeout(warmupRuntimeModels(rebuilt, true), SESSION_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, "session probe");
+        } catch (probeError) {
+          await disposeRuntimeModels(rebuilt, "failed-probe session");

+        }
+        if (stopped) {
+          // A stop landed mid-rebuild — don't leave orphan sessions behind.
+          await disposeRuntimeModels(rebuilt, "superseded rebuilt session");
+          return false;
+        }
+        if (promote && models !== preserved) {
+          // A frame error rebuilt the live set while this candidate was
+          // compiling — discard it rather than stomp the fresh sessions.
+          await disposeRuntimeModels(rebuilt, "orphaned promotion candidate");
+          return false;
+        }
+        models = rebuilt;
+        // The cached detection boxes came from the dead session's frame;

+    if (quiet) {

+  const attemptWebgpuRepromotion = async (): Promise<void> => {

+    }

+        logged: true
+      };

+      emit(payload);

+    }

+function irisInBox(irisCenter: [number, number] | undefined, box: Detection): [number, number] {
+  if (irisCenter === undefined) {
+    return [0, 0];
+  }
+  const [cx, cy] = center(box);
+  const halfW = Math.max(4, width(box) * 0.5);
+  const halfH = Math.max(3, height(box) * 0.5);
+  const ox = Math.max(-1.5, Math.min(1.5, (irisCenter[0] - cx) / halfW));
+  const oy = Math.max(-1.5, Math.min(1.5, (irisCenter[1] - cy) / halfH));
+  return [ox, oy];
+}
+
+// COMETIC-style implicit label: accept a fixated on-screen position only when
+// the current map already lands near it — filters "looked elsewhere" moments.
+function handleImplicitSample(calibration: Calibration, recentFeatures: TimedFeature[], xNorm: number, yNorm: number, pursuitActive: boolean, driftMonitor: DriftMonitor): boolean {
+  if (recentFeatures.length < 3 || pursuitActive) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  if (calibration.featureMap === null && calibration.matrix === null) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  const now = performance.now();
+  const featureAt = now - 250;
+  let best: TimedFeature | null = null;
+  for (const entry of recentFeatures) {
+    if (best === null || Math.abs(entry.at - featureAt) < Math.abs(best.at - featureAt)) {
+      best = entry;
+    }
+  }
+  if (best === null || Math.abs(best.at - featureAt) > 400) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  const target: [number, number] = [clamp01(xNorm), clamp01(yNorm)];
+  const estimate = calibration.applyFeature(best.feature);
+  const offset: [number, number] = [target[0] - estimate[0], target[1] - estimate[1]];
+  const agreed = Math.hypot(offset[0], offset[1]) <= 0.09;
+  const correction = driftMonitor.record(agreed, offset, now, target);
+  if (correction !== null) {
+    const applied = calibration.applyDriftCorrection(correction[0] * 0.85, correction[1] * 0.85);
+    // Match the worker path: escalate at 0.15 cumulative — ~8 sustained
+    // confirmations — not the 0.35 hard bound.
+    const saturated = Math.hypot(applied[0], applied[1]) >= 0.15;
+    console.info("Drift auto-corrected", JSON.stringify({ applied, saturated }));
+    if (saturated) {
+      return true;
+    }
+  }
+  if (!agreed) {
+    // Bounded rejects still carry regional-bias signal: the map predicted a
+    // point within 0.2 of this label — close enough that the miss is the
+    // map's bias, not a look-elsewhere label. Low weight keeps a stray from
+    // steering the field.
+    if (Math.hypot(offset[0], offset[1]) <= 0.2) {
+      calibration.addResidualBiasEvidence(best.feature, target, 0.3);
+    }
+    return false;
+  }
+  calibration.addImplicitSample(best.feature, target);
+  void calibration.refitWithImplicit(now);
+  return false;
+}

+// Returns the resolution the sensor ACTUALLY delivered — under the
+// default-policy fallback that differs from the request, and every
+// downstream consumer (canvas, projector, detector scaling, calibration
+// fingerprint) must key off it rather than the configured dims.
+async function openCamera(
+  camera: string,
+  requested: CameraResolution,
+  gazeMaxFps: number,
+  emit: (payload: BackendMessage) => void,
+  fallback: CameraResolution | null
+): Promise<{ stream: MediaStream; video: HTMLVideoElement; resolution: CameraResolution }> {
+  const constraints = await cameraConstraints(camera);
+  const attempt = async (resolution: CameraResolution) => {
+    // Bounded: a camera that accepts-but-never-delivers must surface as an
+    // error, not wedge boot. If getUserMedia resolves AFTER the deadline
+    // the stream is still real — stop its tracks so the LED doesn't stay
+    // on for a capture nobody drives (same late-settle pattern as the
+    // orphaned InferenceSession cleanup in runtimes.ts).
+    const pending = navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({
+      video: {
+        ...constraints,
+        width: { exact: resolution.width },
+        height: { exact: resolution.height },
+        // ideal (not exact): unusual cameras may not hit the requested rate —
+        // ask politely rather than fail the constraint.
+        frameRate: { ideal: gazeMaxFps > 0 ? gazeMaxFps : 30 }
+      },
+      audio: false
+    });
+    const stream = await withTimeout(pending, CAMERA_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, "camera getUserMedia").catch((error) => {
+      void pending.then(
+        (late) => {
+          for (const track of late.getTracks()) {
+            track.stop();
+          }
+        },
+        () => undefined
+      );
+      throw error;
+    });
+    try {
+      const video = document.createElement("video");
+      video.autoplay = true;
+      video.muted = true;
+      video.playsInline = true;
+      video.srcObject = stream;
+      await withTimeout(video.play(), CAMERA_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, "camera video play");
+      await waitForVideo(video);
+      const settings = stream.getVideoTracks()[0]?.getSettings();
+      const actualWidth = settings?.width ?? video.videoWidth;
+      const actualHeight = settings?.height ?? video.videoHeight;
+      if (actualWidth !== resolution.width || actualHeight !== resolution.height) {
+        throw new Error(`Camera returned ${actualWidth}x${actualHeight}, expected ${resolution.width}x${resolution.height}`);
+      }
+      return { stream, video, resolution };
+    } catch (error) {
+      // A failed attempt must not leak a live capture — the retry or the
+      // caller's error path decides what happens next.
+      for (const track of stream.getTracks()) {
+        track.stop();
+      }
+      throw error;
+    }
+  };
   try {
-    if (validation) await calibration.validate(sample.feature, target);
-    else await calibration.capture(sample.feature, target);
+    return await attempt(requested);
   } catch (error) {
+    if (fallback === null || (fallback.width === requested.width && fallback.height === requested.height)) {
+      throw error;
+    }
     const payload: BackendMessage = {
       type: "status",
-      level: "error",
-      message: `Calibration capture failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
-      runtime: config.runtime,
+      level: "warning",
+      message: `Camera could not deliver ${requested.width}x${requested.height} (${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}); falling back to ${fallback.width}x${fallback.height}`,
+      camera_width: fallback.width,
+      camera_height: fallback.height,
+      camera_resolution_name: fallback.name,
       logged: true
     };
     logStatus(payload, error);
     emit(payload);
+    return attempt(fallback);
   }

 export const GAZE_STALE_MS = 1500;
+export const PREVIEW_STALE_MS = 2000;
 
+// Render-side motion constants. The spring is critically damped — it settles
+// fast without overshoot, so a retargeting frame can't kick the dot past
+// where the eye landed. Feed-forward lead is capped at ~2 frames: pursuit
+// keeps pace, saccades (which arrive snapped, never predicted) can't coast.
+export const DOT_EXTRAPOLATE_MAX_SEC = 0.033;
+export const DOT_SMOOTH_TIME_SEC = 0.1;
+export const DOT_DEADBAND_PX = 1.5;
+// A retarget this large is a saccade — snap, don't chase. ‖Δ‖ in normalized
+// screen units (0.08 ≈ 150px on a 1920-wide display); the upstream gaze_state
+// flag is preferred when present, this is the geometric fallback.
+export const DOT_SNAP_JUMP_NORM = 0.08;
+
+export interface DotMotion {
+  pos: [number, number];
+  vel: [number, number];
+}
+
+// True when the incoming sample is a jump the spring should snap to rather
+// than chase — saccade-marked by the stream, or a jump beyond the norm floor.
+export function isSaccadeJump(
+  state: string | undefined,
+  prev: [number, number] | null,
+  next: [number, number]
+): boolean {
+  if (state === "saccade") {
+    return true;
+  }
+  if (!prev) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  return Math.hypot(next[0] - prev[0], next[1] - prev[1]) > DOT_SNAP_JUMP_NORM;
+}
+
+// Capped feed-forward: shift the chase target along the measured velocity by
+// the sample's age (wall-clock captured_at → includes pipeline latency),
+// clamped to ~2 frames so stale frames can't coast the dot into overshoot.
+export function leadTarget(
+  target: [number, number],
+  vel: [number, number],
+  sinceUpdateSec: number
+): [number, number] {
+  const lead = Math.min(Math.max(sinceUpdateSec, 0), DOT_EXTRAPOLATE_MAX_SEC);
+  return [target[0] + vel[0] * lead, target[1] + vel[1] * lead];
+}
+
+// Critically damped spring step (SmoothDamp without a max-speed cap — the
+// display velocity stays bounded by construction). Unlike the old exponential
+// chase, acceleration is continuous: retargeting produces an ease, not a kick.
+// Parks inside the deadband once the residual AND the drift are both quiet —
+// gating position alone would freeze the dot mid-flight whenever the residual
+// dipped below the deadband.
+export function advanceDotSpring(
+  pos: [number, number],
+  vel: [number, number],
+  target: [number, number],
+  dtSec: number,
+  viewPx: [number, number] = [1920, 1080]
+): DotMotion {
+  const dt = Math.min(Math.max(dtSec, 0), 0.05);
+  if (dt === 0) {
+    return { pos, vel };
+  }
+  const omega = 2 / DOT_SMOOTH_TIME_SEC;
+  const x = omega * dt;
+  const exp = 1 / (1 + x + 0.48 * x * x + 0.235 * x * x * x);
+  const dx = pos[0] - target[0];
+  const dy = pos[1] - target[1];
+  const tx = (vel[0] + omega * dx) * dt;
+  const ty = (vel[1] + omega * dy) * dt;
+  const nvx = (vel[0] - omega * tx) * exp;
+  const nvy = (vel[1] - omega * ty) * exp;
+  const npx = target[0] + (dx + tx) * exp;
+  const npy = target[1] + (dy + ty) * exp;
+  // Deadband the residual to the target (not the frame step) and require the
+  // spring to be quiet — parking on residual alone would freeze mid-flight.
+  const rxPx = (target[0] - pos[0]) * viewPx[0];
+  const ryPx = (target[1] - pos[1]) * viewPx[1];
+  const vPx = Math.hypot(vel[0] * viewPx[0], vel[1] * viewPx[1]);
+  if (Math.hypot(rxPx, ryPx) < DOT_DEADBAND_PX && vPx < 2) {
+    return { pos, vel: [0, 0] };
+  }
+  return { pos: [npx, npy], vel: [nvx, nvy] };
+}
+
+// save_failed comes from commitPending on the pursuit/verify path — the only
+// calibration flow left. The old point-capture statuses (unstable, no_sample)
+// were emitted by the removed capture() path and can no longer arrive.
 export function shouldRetryCalibrationCapture(status: string): boolean {
-  return status === "unstable" || status === "no_sample" || status === "save_failed";
+  return status === "save_failed";
 }
 
 export function scheduleGazeExpiry(receivedAt: number, onExpired: () => void): () => void {
@@ -9,3 +97,32 @@ export function scheduleGazeExpiry(receivedAt: number, onExpired: () => void): (
   const timeoutId = globalThis.setTimeout(onExpired, delay);
   return () => globalThis.clearTimeout(timeoutId);
 }
+
+export function schedulePreviewExpiry(receivedAt: number, onExpired: () => void): () => void {
+  const delay = Math.max(0, receivedAt + PREVIEW_STALE_MS - Date.now());
+  const timeoutId = globalThis.setTimeout(onExpired, delay);
+  return () => globalThis.clearTimeout(timeoutId);
+}
+
+// Head-pose gate for pursuit calibration: a tilted head shifts the
+// eye→screen mapping the fit can't see (the model has no pose input), so
+// capture and verify hold their sample stream while |yaw| or |pitch| sits
+// beyond this limit. 12° sits above ordinary seated drift (~5-8° of
+// micro-motion while fixating) and well short of the gross rotations the
+// stream's head_turned flag catches — tight enough to keep bent-pose frames
+// out of the fit, loose enough that a relaxed user isn't nagged.
+export const HEAD_TILT_LIMIT_DEG = 12;
+// The pose must read level for this long before sampling resumes —
+// hysteresis so one briefly-level frame mid-nod can't reopen the gate.
+export const TILT_CLEAR_MS = 300;
+
+// True when either pose angle exceeds the limit. Missing or non-finite
+// angles never block: absent telemetry means we can't know the pose, not
+// that it's bad — a frame without head pose must not stall calibration.
+export function headTilted(yawDeg?: number, pitchDeg?: number, opts?: { thresholdDeg?: number }): boolean {
+  const limit = opts?.thresholdDeg ?? HEAD_TILT_LIMIT_DEG;
+  return (
+    (yawDeg !== undefined && Number.isFinite(yawDeg) && Math.abs(yawDeg) > limit) ||
+    (pitchDeg !== undefined && Number.isFinite(pitchDeg) && Math.abs(pitchDeg) > limit)
+  );
+}

     public init(directory: URL) {

-        if let data = try? Data(contentsOf: fileURL),
-           let agents = try? JSONDecoder().decode([CompanionAgent].self, from: data) {

     }
 
+    /// One malformed record must not zero the roster — decode wholesale
+    /// first; on failure fall back to element-wise salvage so valid agents
+    /// survive a corrupt sibling. Every dropped record is logged by what
+    /// little identity it carried.
+    static func loadRoster(from data: Data) -> [CompanionAgent] {
+        if let agents = try? JSONDecoder().decode([CompanionAgent].self, from: data) {
+            return agents
+        }
+        guard let raw = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [Any] else {
+            Self.log.error("agents.json is unreadable — roster left empty rather than guessed")
+            return []
+        }
+        var dropped: [String] = []
+        let agents = raw.compactMap { element -> CompanionAgent? in
+            guard let slice = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: element),
+                  let agent = try? JSONDecoder().decode(CompanionAgent.self, from: slice)
+            else {
+                let identity = (element as? [String: Any])
+                    .flatMap { $0["slug"] ?? $0["name"] } as? String ?? "<unidentified>"
+                dropped.append(identity)
+                return nil
+            }
+            return agent
+        }
+        for slug in dropped {
+            Self.log.error("agents.json dropped a malformed record: \(slug, privacy: .public)")
+        }
+        return agents
+    }
+

+        var stopped: [String] = []
+        var missed: [String] = []
+        for slug in slugs.sorted() {
+            let name = agents.first(where: { $0.slug == slug })?.name ?? slug
+            do {
+                if try await runtime.interrupt(slug: slug) {
+                    stopped.append(name)
+                } else {
+                    missed.append(name)
+                }
+            } catch {
+                missed.append(name)
+            }
+        }
+        if stopped.isEmpty {
+            return VoiceToolResult(status: VoiceToolResult.Status.nothingRunning,
+                say: "The agents already stopped.").encoded()
         }
+        let spoken = "Stopped \(VoiceToolResult.spoken(stopped.joined(separator: ", "), words: 8))"
+        return VoiceToolResult(
+            status: VoiceToolResult.Status.cancelled,
+            say: missed.isEmpty ? spoken
+                : "\(spoken); \(missed.count) already finished").encoded()
     }

-    /// The drive loop executes one spec to a `DriveResult`; statuses map to

+    /// Transcript bound — long sessions used to grow `messages` forever,
+    /// making every render re-walk the whole history. Pruning shifts
+    /// `streamingItems` indices, so the map is re-based with the drop.
+    static let messageCap = 500
+
+    private static func capped(_ transcript: AgentChat) -> AgentChat {
+        var transcript = transcript
+        let overflow = transcript.messages.count - messageCap
+        guard overflow > 0 else { return transcript }
+        transcript.messages.removeFirst(overflow)
+        // Indices below the cut point to evicted rows — drop them so a
+        // streaming item can't re-anchor to the wrong message.
+        transcript.streamingItems = transcript.streamingItems.reduce(into: [:]) { out, pair in
+            let shifted = pair.value - overflow
+            if shifted >= 0 { out[pair.key] = shifted }
+        }
+        return transcript
+    }
+

 /// focused element (element-scoped, no keystrokes); when no editable element
 /// answers, falls back to clipboard+⌘V, which snapshots every pasteboard
 /// item's types and restores them after the target has read the paste.
+///
+/// The transcript runs through a small editing vocabulary first — "new
+/// line" inserts a newline, "scratch that" deletes the last inserted
+/// segment, "undo that" removes the last whole delivery, and "delete
+/// last sentence" cuts back to the previous sentence boundary. Plain
+/// text still lands through the same insert → paste path.

+    /// (`inputGuard = DictationDelivery.sharedLease`), so a drive-loop
+    /// focus borrow or clipboard_write can never interleave with a
+    /// dictation ⌘V+restore. One lease is the whole guarantee;

+    /// One editing action parsed from a transcript — `insert` carries a
+    /// literal segment (newlines included), the rest are removals.
+    /// Internal for tests.
+    enum EditToken: Equatable {
+        case insert(String), scratch, undo, deleteSentence
+    }
+
+    /// Transcript → editing actions. Command phrases match
+    /// case-insensitively on word boundaries with surrounding punctuation
+    /// ignored; unmatched runs join into one insert each. Commands work
+    /// standalone or mid-utterance — "one new line two" is a line, a
+    /// newline, another line. Internal for tests.
+    static func editTokens(_ transcript: String) -> [EditToken] {
+        var tokens: [EditToken] = []
+        var pending: [String] = []
+        func flush() {
+            guard !pending.isEmpty else { return }
+            tokens.append(.insert(pending.joined(separator: " ")))
+            pending = []
+        }
+        let words = transcript.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace)
+        func stripped(_ word: Substring) -> String {
+            String(word).lowercased()
+                .trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet.alphanumerics.inverted)
+        }
+        var i = words.startIndex
+        while i < words.endIndex {
+            let rest = words[i...]
+            if rest.count >= 3,
+               stripped(rest[rest.startIndex]) == "delete",
+               stripped(rest[rest.index(after: rest.startIndex)]) == "last",
+               stripped(rest[rest.index(rest.startIndex, offsetBy: 2)]) == "sentence" {
+                flush(); tokens.append(.deleteSentence)
+                i = rest.index(rest.startIndex, offsetBy: 3); continue
+            }
+            if rest.count >= 2 {
+                let first = stripped(rest[rest.startIndex])
+                let second = stripped(rest[rest.index(after: rest.startIndex)])
+                if first == "scratch", second == "that" {
+                    flush(); tokens.append(.scratch)
+                    i = rest.index(rest.startIndex, offsetBy: 2); continue
+                }
+                if first == "undo", second == "that" {
+                    flush(); tokens.append(.undo)
+                    i = rest.index(rest.startIndex, offsetBy: 2); continue
+                }
+                if first == "new", second == "line" {
+                    flush(); tokens.append(.insert("\n"))
+                    i = rest.index(rest.startIndex, offsetBy: 2); continue
+                }
+            }
+            if stripped(rest[rest.startIndex]) == "newline" {
+                flush(); tokens.append(.insert("\n"))
+                i = rest.index(after: rest.startIndex); continue
+            }
+            pending.append(String(rest[rest.startIndex]))
+            i = rest.index(after: rest.startIndex)
+        }
+        flush()
+        return tokens
+    }

+    /// What got inserted, oldest first — units split at every vocabulary
+    /// command, and each deliver() call stamps its own group so "undo
+    /// that" can remove a whole utterance while "scratch that" removes
+    /// just the last piece. Deletions ride Character counts, matching the
+    /// delete-keystroke seam.
+    final class EditHistory: @unchecked Sendable {
+        private let lock = NSLock()
+        private var units: [(group: Int, text: String)] = []
+        private var nextGroup = 0
+        /// Cap the ledger — a segment forgotten beats deleting stale text
+        /// from a field the user has edited by hand since.
+        private static let unitCap = 200
+
+        func beginGroup() -> Int {
+            lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
+            let group = nextGroup; nextGroup += 1
+            return group
+        }
+        func record(_ text: String, group: Int) {
+            guard !text.isEmpty else { return }
+            lock.lock()
+            units.append((group, text))
+            if units.count > Self.unitCap { units.removeFirst(units.count - Self.unitCap) }
+            lock.unlock()
+        }
+        /// "scratch that" — the last single unit's Character count.
+        func popLast() -> Int {
+            lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
+            guard let last = units.popLast() else { return 0 }
+            return last.text.count
+        }
+        /// "undo that" — every unit of the most recent delivery.
+        func popLastGroup() -> Int {
+            lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
+            guard let group = units.last?.group else { return 0 }
+            var chars = 0
+            while let last = units.last, last.group == group {
+                chars += last.text.count
+                units.removeLast()
+            }
+            return chars
+        }
+        /// "delete last sentence" — the trailing fragment after the last
+        /// sentence boundary (. ! ? or newline) that still has text
+        /// following it; no usable boundary means the whole history is
+        /// one sentence.
+        func popSentence() -> Int {
+            lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
+            let full = units.map(\.text).joined()
+            guard let lastText = full.lastIndex(where: { !Self.isTerminator($0) }) else {
+                let n = full.count
+                units.removeAll()
+                return n
+            }
+            let head = full[..<lastText]
+            guard let boundary = head.lastIndex(where: { Self.isTerminator($0) }) else {
+                let n = full.count
+                units.removeAll()
+                return n
+            }
+            return popChars(full.distance(from: full.index(after: boundary), to: full.endIndex))
+        }
+        private static func isTerminator(_ c: Character) -> Bool {
+            c == "." || c == "!" || c == "?" || c == "\n"
+        }
+        /// Removes `n` trailing Characters across units — the top unit
+        /// may be only partly consumed, so trim it in place.
+        private func popChars(_ n: Int) -> Int {
+            var need = n, removed = 0
+            while need > 0, let last = units.last {
+                if last.text.count <= need {
+                    removed += last.text.count
+                    need -= last.text.count
+                    units.removeLast()
+                } else {
+                    var trimmed = last.text
+                    trimmed.removeLast(need)
+                    units[units.count - 1] = (last.group, trimmed)
+                    removed += need
+                    need = 0
+                }
+            }
+            return removed
+        }
     }

+    /// Cancellation-aware acquire. AsyncLease hands a released lease to
+    /// its oldest parked waiter regardless of that waiter's cancellation,
+    /// so abandoning the await isn't enough — when cancel wins the race,
+    /// the still-landing acquire must hand the lease straight on or
+    /// `held` would stay true forever and every later delivery wedges.
+    private static func acquireSharedLease() async -> Bool {
+        guard !Task.isCancelled else { return false }
+        let race = DeliveryRace()
+        Task {
+            await Self.sharedLease.acquire()
+            if !race.finish(true) {
+                // The waiter left before the handoff — we own the lease
+                // now; pass it to the next waiter (or mark it free).
+                await Self.sharedLease.release()
+            }
+        }
+        return await race.result(fallback: false)
+    }
+
+    /// First-finisher race — the same shape as VoiceController's
+    /// CancellationRace; a small duplicate beats reaching across lanes
+    /// for a helper.
+    private final class DeliveryRace: @unchecked Sendable {
+        private let lock = NSLock()
+        private var continuation: CheckedContinuation<Bool, Never>?
+        private var outcome: Bool?
+        private var settled = false
+        /// Returns false when the race was already settled — the result
+        /// goes unconsumed and the caller owns whatever it represented.
+        @discardableResult
+        func finish(_ value: Bool) -> Bool {
+            lock.lock()
+            if settled { lock.unlock(); return false }
+            settled = true; outcome = value
+            let pending = continuation; continuation = nil
+            lock.unlock()
+            pending?.resume(returning: value)
+            return true
+        }
+        func result(fallback: Bool) async -> Bool {
+            await withTaskCancellationHandler {
+                await withCheckedContinuation { (c: CheckedContinuation<Bool, Never>) in
+                    lock.lock()
+                    if settled, let outcome { lock.unlock(); c.resume(returning: outcome) }
+                    else { continuation = c; lock.unlock() }
+                }
+            } onCancel: { finish(fallback) }
+        }
+    }

+    /// The drive lane's dictation verbs land here — `onDictationRequest`
+    /// hands a Bool ("start"/"stop dictating") and this reports whether
+    /// the request actually took effect, so the loop's "Dictation is
+    /// on"/"isn't available" lines stay honest: the feature gate off, an
+    /// already-latched start, and a stop with nothing running all have
+    /// their own truthful answers instead of a claimed toggle.
+    func dictationRequest(_ start: Bool) -> Bool {
+        if start {
+            guard config.dictationHotkey else { return false }
+            // Idempotent like `startDictation` — a second "start
+            // dictating" while one runs reports the live state, not a
+            // toggle-off.

+        // reaches this lane; a tap on Fn is its documented stop anyway.
+        guard voiceLatched else { return false }
+        voiceLatched = false
+        finish()
+        return true
+    }

+    /// Bounded chain-wait for the microphone task serialisation — a prior
+    /// prepare parked on a dead wait (continuation that never resumes)
+    /// must not chain-wedge every later preparation forever. Past the
+    /// bound the caller abandons the chain; the lane skips re-joining a
+    /// stale preparation on its own side.
+    private static func awaitChained(_ task: Task<Void, Never>?, timeout: TimeInterval = 10) async {
+        guard let task else { return }
+        let race = CancellationRace<Void>()
+        Task { race.finish(await task.value) }
+        let timer = Task {
+            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(timeout))
+            race.finish(())
+        }
+        await race.result(fallback: ())
+        timer.cancel()
+    }

+    /// One wiring pass per runtime — reply/event/cursor sinks, the agent
+    //  UI binding, and the per-agent MCP stdio server surface.
+    private func wireAgentRuntime(_ runtime: AgentRuntime) {
+        runtime.onAgentReply = { [weak self] _, text in
+            // Agent replies are documents — speak a bounded lead, not the whole
+            // thing. Push as a task_outcome so the lane voices `say` verbatim
+            // instead of answering bare text as if it were a question.
+            let lead = String((text.split(separator: ".").first.map(String.init) ?? text).prefix(200))
+            let say = VoiceToolResult.spoken(lead, words: 30)
+            let payload = VoiceToolResult(
+                kind: VoiceToolResult.Kind.taskOutcome,
+                status: VoiceToolResult.Status.ok,
+                say: say.isEmpty ? "The agent replied." : say).encoded()
+            if self?.controller.voiceAgentEvent(payload) != true {
+                self?.speechOutput.speak(lead)
+            }
+        }
+        // Each agent's codex gets a stdio MCP server entry — the same
+        // binary re-execed as `JevVoice --mcp-stdio --agent <slug>` — plus
+        // TYPESAFE_API_KEY in its environment so codex's `env_vars`
+        // pass-through hands it to the MCP child without touching disk.
+        // The key is read live at spawn so a mid-session key set works.
+        runtime.start(
+            mcpServersFor: { agent in
+                [CodexMCPServer(name: "jev-drive",
+                                command: Bundle.main.executablePath
+                                    ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.arguments[0],
+                                args: ["--mcp-stdio", "--agent", agent.slug],
+                                envVars: ["TYPESAFE_API_KEY"],
+                                cwd: agent.workspacePath)]
+            },
+            environmentFor: { _ in ["TYPESAFE_API_KEY": Config.shared.apiKey] })
+        // The runtime owns the single event-stream consumer, fanning
+        // events out to the UI here.
+        windows.agents.bind(roster: runtime.store, runtime: runtime)
+        runtime.onAgentEvent = { [weak self] event in
+            self?.windows.agents.handle(event)
+        }
+        // Name chips track each agent session's drawn cursor — the
+        // driver draws the cursor, the app labels whose it is.
+        controller.cua.cursorLabelSink = { [weak self] slug, point in
+            guard let self else { return }
+            if let point {
+                self.windows.cursorLabels.show(runtime.cursor(for: slug), at: point)
+            } else {
+                self.windows.cursorLabels.hide(agentSlug: slug)
+            }
+        }

+    /// Composition-seam + local-intelligence wiring.
+    ///
+    ///   - `controller.gazeTapHandler` → `GazeService.commitTarget` +
+    ///     `cua.actuateCommitted`: a speechless Fn tap (sub-100ms of
+    ///     audio) commits the referent under the eyes instead of the
+    ///     silent dismiss. The voice lane fires it only for a tap that
+    ///     sent audio upstream; `config.tapToGazeClick` is read inside
+    ///     the handler so the Settings toggle needs no restart.
+    ///   - `controller.cancelAllTasks` → `cua.cancelAllRunning()`: the
+    ///     universal stop — Escape settles every voice task, parked ask,
+    ///     and in-flight agent turn, not just the capture.
+    ///   - `controller.localSpeechSink` → `LocalTranscriber.ingest` and
+    ///     `controller.localSpeechWindow` → `start()`/`stop()`: the tee
+    ///     hears the same converted PCM the socket does; the window hook
+    ///     brackets each capture so the transcriber's turn matches the
+    ///     hold. Gates: `localSTTEnabled` or `commandSpottingEnabled`
+    ///     open the tap; the live flags are re-read per sink/hook call.
+    ///   - `localRouter` — on partials it may speculatively dispatch
+    ///     reversible-safe actions and always enforces stop-words; on
+    ///     finals it routes through `handleLocalCommand` (the
+    ///     coordinator's normal admission), claims consumed utterances
+    ///     so the realtime lane's same-audio tool call can't re-run
+    ///     them, and hands needs-remote goals a last shot at a parked
+    ///     ask before the remote model owns them. Gate:
+    ///     `commandSpottingEnabled`.
+    ///   - `controller.speaker` → `LocalVoice.shared` once its models
+    ///     are ready (PocketTTS downloads on first prepare); the
+    ///     `ttsEnabled` toggle-off restores `speechOutput`, and any
+    ///     prepare failure leaves the AVSpeech lane in place.
+    ///   - `localChooserEnabled` is consumed inside the coordinator's
+    ///     DriveLoop construction — per-task read, no wiring here.
+    private func wireLocalIntelligence() {
+        controller.gazeTapHandler = { [weak self] in
+            guard let self, await self.controller.config.tapToGazeClick
+            else { return false }
+            guard let (candidate, _) = await GazeService.shared.commitTarget()
+            else { return false }
+            return await self.controller.cua.actuateCommitted(candidate)
+        }
+        // Universal stop — Escape lands on every lane: running tasks,
+        // parked asks (a cancel resolves their continuation like the
+        // deadline does), and agent turns in flight.
+        controller.cancelAllTasks = { [weak self] in
+            _ = await self?.controller.cua.cancelAllRunning()
+        }
+        controller.localSpeechWindow = { [weak self] open in
+            self?.applyLocalSpeechWindow(open)
+        }
+        let router = localRouter
+        // Dispatches re-enter the coordinator's ordinary admission —
+        // consent, deny scans, claims, and the task ledger are shared,
+        // never a shortcut lane.
+        router.onCommand = { [weak self] command in
+            guard let self else { return }
+            _ = await self.controller.cua.handleLocalCommand(
+                command, isPartial: command.isPartialSpeculation)
+        }
+        // The router consumed these words; the realtime model heard the
+        // same audio and its tool-call echo must not re-run them.
+        router.onConsumed = { [weak self] transcript in
+            Task { @MainActor in self?.controller.cua.noteLocalClaim(transcript) }
+        }
+        router.onCancel = { [weak self] in
+            Task { _ = await self?.controller.cua.cancelAllRunning() }
+        }
+        // The grammar can't express this — but a parked ask may be
+        // waiting on exactly these words ("yes", "two", "always for
+        // Safari" never parse as commands). Only after the ask declines
+        // them does the remote lane own the utterance — it heard the
+        // audio itself, so there is nothing extra to send.
+        router.onNeedsRemote = { [weak self] goal in

+            }

+        Publishers.CombineLatest(controller.config.$localSTTEnabled,
+                                 controller.config.$commandSpottingEnabled)

+            .store(in: &subscriptions)
+        // Local voice — adopt only after its models are really present
+        // (first prepare downloads them); AVSpeech stays the fallback.
+        controller.config.$ttsEnabled
+            .sink { [weak self] on in
+                guard let self else { return }
+                if !on {
+                    self.controller.speaker = self.speechOutput
+                    return

+                Task { [weak self] in

+                    // download shouldn't wake the lane anyway.
+                    if self.controller.config.ttsEnabled {
+                        self.controller.speaker = LocalVoice.shared
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            .store(in: &subscriptions)

+    private func paintEyes(hostState: TrackerHost.State) {
+        // Every repaint re-picks the affordance set — a state that hid an
+        // item last pass can't strand it hidden in the next.
+        eyesEnable?.isEnabled = true
+        switch hostState {
+        case .starting:
+            eyesHeader?.title = "Eyes — Starting…"
+            // The affordance stays visible but disabled: the honest state
+            // is "a start is already in flight", not "the feature is gone".
+            eyesEnable?.isHidden = false
+            eyesEnable?.isEnabled = false
+            eyesRestart?.isHidden = true
+            eyesPause?.isHidden = true
+            eyesRecalibrate?.isHidden = true
+        case .failed(let message):
+            eyesHeader?.title = "Eyes — Stopped (\(Self.shortTrackerFailure(message)))"
+            eyesEnable?.isHidden = true
+            eyesRestart?.isHidden = false
+            eyesPause?.isHidden = true
+            eyesRecalibrate?.isHidden = true
+        case .stopped:
+            eyesHeader?.title = "Eyes — Off"
+            eyesEnable?.isHidden = false
+            eyesRestart?.isHidden = true
+            eyesPause?.isHidden = true
+            eyesRecalibrate?.isHidden = true
+        case .running:
+            eyesHeader?.title = eyesStatus.map { "Eyes — \($0.label)" } ?? "Eyes — Running"
+            eyesEnable?.isHidden = true
+            eyesRestart?.isHidden = true
+            if let status = eyesStatus {
+                eyesPause?.isHidden = false
+                eyesPause?.title = status.paused ? "Resume Tracking" : "Pause Tracking"
+                eyesRecalibrate?.isHidden = false
+            } else {
+                // Host reports running but /snapshot hasn't landed yet —
+                // pause/recalibrate would just post to a dead socket.
+                eyesPause?.isHidden = true
+                eyesRecalibrate?.isHidden = true
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    /// Menu titles stay short: keep the first clause of the failure reason
+    /// (the messages all start "The eye tracker …") and cap the length.
+    private static func shortTrackerFailure(_ message: String) -> String {
+        var first = message.components(separatedBy: ".").first ?? message
+        for prefix in ["The eye tracker ", "the eye tracker "] {
+            if first.hasPrefix(prefix) { first.removeFirst(prefix.count) }
+        }
+        let trimmed = first.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        return trimmed.count > 48 ? String(trimmed.prefix(47)) + "…" : trimmed
+    }
